views.name: posts_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostTypeId,
  AcceptedAnswerId,
  CreaionDate,
  Score,
  ViewCount,
  Body,
  OwnerUserId,
  LasActivityDate,
  Title,
  Tags,
  AnswerCount,
  CommentCount,
  FavoriteCount,
  LastEditorUserId,
  LastEditDate,
  CommunityOwnedDate,
  ParentId,
  ClosedDate,
  OwnerDisplayName,
  LastEditorDisplayName,
  -- derived useful flags/measures
  (CASE WHEN ParentId IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_question,
  (CASE WHEN ParentId IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS is_answer,
  (LENGTH(Tags) - LENGTH(REPLACE(Tags, '<', ''))) AS tag_token_count
FROM posts

params.description: Provides one-row-per-post basic attributes and simple derived flags/tallies for composing post-level queries (questions or answers).
params.when_to_use: Fetch attributes of a specific post by Id or list of Ids (title, body, author, counts, dates). | Analyze or filter posts by being a question vs an answer (is_question / is_answer). | Filter or bucket posts by tag counts (tag_token_count) or inspect raw Tags string. | Build further aggregations at the post grain (e.g., join to votes/comments aggregates, compute author-level aggregates) without re-scanning the posts base table. | Serve as the canonical post-level input when composing joins to dimensions (users, tags lookup, links) or when layering additional aggregations (comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg).
params.output_schema: Id: post identifier, from posts.Id | PostTypeId: post type code (question/answer/etc), from posts.PostTypeId | AcceptedAnswerId: Id of accepted answer for a question, from posts.AcceptedAnswerId | CreaionDate: creation timestamp of the post (note: column name as in view), from posts.CreaionDate | Score: score (net votes) of the post, from posts.Score | ViewCount: times the post was viewed, from posts.ViewCount | Body: full post body text/HTML, from posts.Body | OwnerUserId: numeric id of the post owner (nullable for deleted/anonymous), from posts.OwnerUserId | LasActivityDate: last activity timestamp for the post (note: column name as in view), from posts.LasActivityDate | Title: post title (primarily for questions), from posts.Title | Tags: raw tag string in angle-bracket format, from posts.Tags | AnswerCount: number of answers (as stored on the posts row), from posts.AnswerCount | CommentCount: number of comments (as stored on the posts row), from posts.CommentCount | FavoriteCount: number of favorites/bookmarks, from posts.FavoriteCount | LastEditorUserId: user id of the last editor (nullable), from posts.LastEditorUserId | LastEditDate: timestamp of the last edit (nullable), from posts.LastEditDate | CommunityOwnedDate: timestamp when community ownership started (nullable), from posts.CommunityOwnedDate | ParentId: parent post id (non-null for answers; null for top-level questions), from posts.ParentId | ClosedDate: timestamp when the question was closed (nullable), from posts.ClosedDate | OwnerDisplayName: display name provided by the owner (nullable), from posts.OwnerDisplayName | LastEditorDisplayName: display name of last editor (nullable), from posts.LastEditorDisplayName | is_question: derived binary flag (1 if ParentId IS NULL else 0) indicating row is a question | is_answer: derived binary flag (1 if ParentId IS NOT NULL else 0) indicating row is an answer | tag_token_count: integer count of tag tokens computed as (LENGTH(Tags) - LENGTH(REPLACE(Tags, '<', ''))), derived from posts.Tags
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.PostTypeId | posts.AcceptedAnswerId | posts.CreaionDate | posts.Score | posts.ViewCount | posts.Body | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.LasActivityDate | posts.Title | posts.Tags | posts.AnswerCount | posts.CommentCount | posts.FavoriteCount | posts.LastEditorUserId | posts.LastEditDate | posts.CommunityOwnedDate | posts.ParentId | posts.ClosedDate | posts.OwnerDisplayName | posts.LastEditorDisplayName
params.metric: is_question = CASE WHEN posts.ParentId IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | is_answer = CASE WHEN posts.ParentId IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END | tag_token_count = (LENGTH(posts.Tags) - LENGTH(REPLACE(posts.Tags, '<', '')))
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner on posts_basic.OwnerUserId = posts_with_owner.Id — safe because posts_with_owner is a one-row-per-user enrichment (JOIN) keyed by user id; joining will not duplicate post-level measures as long as posts_with_owner remains 1:1 per user. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup using a tag token (only after normalizing Tags into one-row-per-tag) — do NOT join tags_lookup directly to posts_basic on the raw Tags string because tags_lookup is one-row-per-tag; you must first turn posts_basic.Tags into rows (explode) or join through a mapping that is one-row-per-post-per-tag and then aggregate back to post if you need post-level metrics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to postlinks_edges on posts_basic.Id = postlinks_edges.SourceId or TargetId — safe only when postlinks_edges is guaranteed to be 0/1 per post for the intended relation; if postlinks_edges is one-to-many, join will multiply post rows and you must aggregate postlinks_edges first (e.g., count links per post) before joining to preserve post-level cardinality. | do NOT join directly to comments_per_post_agg or votes_per_post_agg without aligning on post Id and understanding their grain: instead prefer joining to comments_per_post_agg (aggregated one-row-per-post) on Id — this is safe because comments_per_post_agg is an aggregate view at post-grain. Do NOT join to the raw comments or votes tables (one-to-many) without aggregating to post first, as that would duplicate post-level measures. | do NOT join to user_badge_counts (aggregate per user) in a way that multiplies rows: joining posts_basic.OwnerUserId = user_badge_counts.UserId is safe because user_badge_counts is one-row-per-user; avoid joining to a badges table that is one-to-many per user without aggregating badges to user-level first. | when composing with rank views (latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank): these are per-post rank outputs — joining on Id is safe if the rank view is one-row-per-post (or one-row-per-post-per-rank where rank is unique); verify the sibling view's grain before joining to avoid duplication. | general rule: posts_basic is strictly one-row-per-post (grain = ['Id']). Any join to a view or table that is one-to-many relative to post (e.g., comments table, votes table, postlinks with multiple edges, tags exploded table) will multiply post rows and any non-id measures must be re-aggregated (sum/avg/etc) or the many-side must be reduced to one-row-per-post before joining.

views.description: Normalized projection of posts keeping original post attributes, canonicalizing obvious typos in column names and exposing boolean flags and parsed tag counts. Use this as the cleaned posts relation for downstream joins and aggregations. | Use for: Count questions vs answers, filter by tag count or tag membership (downstream parsing), join to users for owner attributes, compute aggregates per user or per tag; Identify unanswered questions (AnswerCount = 0) or closed questions (ClosedDate IS NOT NULL); Time-based analysis of post creation or activity using CreaionDate and LasActivityDate
validated_on: What is the display name of the user who last edited the post "Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation"?

views.name: posts_with_owner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id,
  p.PostTypeId,
  p.AcceptedAnswerId,
  p.CreaionDate,
  p.Score,
  p.ViewCount,
  p.Body,
  p.OwnerUserId,
  p.LasActivityDate,
  p.Title,
  p.Tags,
  p.AnswerCount,
  p.CommentCount,
  p.FavoriteCount,
  p.LastEditorUserId,
  p.LastEditDate,
  p.CommunityOwnedDate,
  p.ParentId,
  p.ClosedDate,
  p.OwnerDisplayName,
  p.LastEditorDisplayName,
  u.Id AS user_Id,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate,
  u.WebsiteUrl AS WebsiteUrl,
  u.Location AS Location,
  u.AboutMe AS AboutMe,
  u.Views AS Views,
  u.UpVotes AS UpVotes,
  u.DownVotes AS DownVotes,
  u.AccountId AS AccountId,
  u.Age AS Age,
  u.ProfileImageUrl AS ProfileImageUrl
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id

params.description: A left-joined view of posts with their owner user row flattened in; answers questions about posts enriched with the owning user's attributes.
params.when_to_use: Fetch post-level details together with the owner's profile (e.g., display name, reputation, profile url). | Filter or group by post attributes while showing user metadata (e.g., top-scoring questions with owner's reputation). | Build further aggregates at the post grain (e.g., join to comment or vote aggregates keyed by post id). | Serve as a normalized post-level starting point for reporting, UI read models, or subsequent safe joins to 1:1 or aggregated data.
params.output_schema: Id: post Id — from posts.Id (this view's grain; one row per posts.Id) | PostTypeId: type of post (question/answer) — from posts.PostTypeId | AcceptedAnswerId: accepted answer post id for a question — from posts.AcceptedAnswerId | CreaionDate: original post creation timestamp (note: column name misspelled in view) — from posts.CreaionDate | Score: numeric score of the post — from posts.Score | ViewCount: number of views for the post — from posts.ViewCount | Body: full body/content of the post — from posts.Body | OwnerUserId: foreign key reference to users.Id for the post owner (nullable for anonymous owners) — from posts.OwnerUserId | LasActivityDate: last activity timestamp on the post (note: column name as in posts) — from posts.LasActivityDate | Title: post title (for questions) — from posts.Title | Tags: tags string on the post (for questions) — from posts.Tags | AnswerCount: number of answers (post-level counter) — from posts.AnswerCount | CommentCount: number of comments on the post — from posts.CommentCount | FavoriteCount: number of favorites/bookmarks — from posts.FavoriteCount | LastEditorUserId: user id of last editor (nullable) — from posts.LastEditorUserId | LastEditDate: timestamp of last edit (nullable) — from posts.LastEditDate | CommunityOwnedDate: timestamp when post became community-owned (nullable) — from posts.CommunityOwnedDate | ParentId: parent post id (for answers) — from posts.ParentId | ClosedDate: timestamp when question was closed (nullable) — from posts.ClosedDate | OwnerDisplayName: display name stored on the post for anonymous/legacy owners — from posts.OwnerDisplayName | LastEditorDisplayName: display name of last editor stored on the post (nullable) — from posts.LastEditorDisplayName | user_Id: owner user's id from users table (same as OwnerUserId when OwnerUserId is not null) — from users.Id (aliased user_Id) | Reputation: owner's reputation score — from users.Reputation | CreationDate: owner's user account creation date — from users.CreationDate | DisplayName: owner's current display name from users table — from users.DisplayName | LastAccessDate: owner's last access timestamp — from users.LastAccessDate | WebsiteUrl: owner's website url from profile — from users.WebsiteUrl | Location: owner's profile location text — from users.Location | AboutMe: owner's about-me html/text — from users.AboutMe | Views: total profile view count for the owner — from users.Views | UpVotes: owner's upvote count (profile metric) — from users.UpVotes | DownVotes: owner's downvote count (profile metric) — from users.DownVotes | AccountId: cross-site account id for the owner (nullable) — from users.AccountId | Age: owner's age from profile (nullable) — from users.Age | ProfileImageUrl: URL to owner's profile image — from users.ProfileImageUrl
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.PostTypeId | posts.AcceptedAnswerId | posts.CreaionDate | posts.Score | posts.ViewCount | posts.Body | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.LasActivityDate | posts.Title | posts.Tags | posts.AnswerCount | posts.CommentCount | posts.FavoriteCount | posts.LastEditorUserId | posts.LastEditDate | posts.CommunityOwnedDate | posts.ParentId | posts.ClosedDate | posts.OwnerDisplayName | posts.LastEditorDisplayName | users.Id | users.Reputation | users.CreationDate | users.DisplayName | users.LastAccessDate | users.WebsiteUrl | users.Location | users.AboutMe | users.Views | users.UpVotes | users.DownVotes | users.AccountId | users.Age | users.ProfileImageUrl
params.metric: This view contains no newly computed aggregate measures; all columns are direct projections from base tables. | Derived metrics should be defined by the query planner or downstream queries. Example helpful definitions to reuse when composing: | post_row_count = COUNT(posts.Id) — basic row-count at this view's grain | post_score_sum = SUM(posts.Score) — sum of Score over posts.Id groups (only valid when grouping by posts.Id or higher-level grouping) | owner_reputation = users.Reputation — direct attribute, not an aggregate
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic on posts.Id = posts_basic.Id — safe because posts_basic is normalized to one row per post.Id (no duplication of this view's post-level measures). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_posthistory_per_post on Id = post_id (assuming latest_posthistory_per_post has at most one row per post) — safe if that sibling view is one-row-per-post (RANK version typically is); verify its rank tie-breaker produces a single row. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to top_posts_by_score_rank on Id = post_id — safe when that ranked view has one row per post (no duplicates). | DO NOT directly join to comments_per_post_agg on posts.Id = comments_per_post_agg.PostId without verifying the sibling is aggregated to one row per post — comments_per_post_agg is an AGG expected to be one-row-per-post and is safe; only join raw comments table (one-to-many) if you re-aggregate to post-level first. | DO NOT join to votes_per_post_agg (if it were pre-aggregated to one row per post, it is safe). Avoid joining to any raw one-to-many tables (e.g., postlinks_edges if it contains multiple edges per post) without first aggregating or deduplicating to the post.Id grain because that will multiply post-level measures such as Score or ViewCount. | Specific guidance for sibling views listed: | - comments_per_post_agg (AGG): safe to join on Id = PostId because it is aggregated to one row per post. | - votes_per_post_agg (AGG): safe to join on Id = PostId when it is aggregated to one row per post. | - user_badge_counts (AGG): safe to join on user_Id = users.Id (one row per user) — does not duplicate post rows if the badge counts view is one-row-per-user. | - postlinks_edges (JOIN): likely one-to-many (edges). Do NOT join directly unless you want to expand posts to multiple link rows; instead aggregate edges to post-level first (e.g., COUNT(*) per post) and then join. | - tags_lookup (NORM): safe to join when tags_lookup is one row per tag key; but if tags_lookup joins to posts producing multiple rows per post, ensure aggregation or string-lookup that preserves one row per post before joining. | General rule: this view's measures are safe to preserve only when downstream joins are 1:1 or many-to-1 onto this view's primary key posts.Id (or onto users.Id for owner-level augmentation). Any many-to- many or 1:many joins must be converted into aggregates (one-row-per-post or one-row-per-user) before joining to avoid duplicating counts/sums present in this view.

views.description: Denormalized posts joined to their owner user record. Preserves both post and user identifiers and common user attributes for downstream filtering and aggregation by user. Useful for owner-level analyses of posts. | Use for: Analyze post quality by owner reputation or activity; Filter posts where owner has low reputation or specific location; Aggregate post counts, scores, or views per user

views.name: comments_per_post_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PostId,
  COUNT(*) AS comment_count,
  AVG(Score) AS comment_avg_score,
  MIN(CreationDate) AS first_comment_date,
  MAX(CreationDate) AS last_comment_date
FROM comments
GROUP BY PostId

params.description: Aggregate comment-level metrics per PostId (count, average score, first and last comment dates).
params.when_to_use: How many comments does a post have? | What is the average score of comments on a post? | When was the first/last comment for a given post? | As a building block when joining post-level comment aggregates to post metadata or other per-post metrics (safe for one-row-per-post composition).
params.output_schema: PostId: identifier of the post that received comments; derived from comments.PostId (GROUP BY key) | comment_count: total number of comment rows for that PostId; derived from COUNT(*) over comments grouped by comments.PostId | comment_avg_score: average of the Score values for comments of that PostId; derived from AVG(comments.Score) over the same group | first_comment_date: earliest CreationDate among comments for that PostId; derived from MIN(comments.CreationDate) | last_comment_date: latest CreationDate among comments for that PostId; derived from MAX(comments.CreationDate)
params.metric: comment_count = COUNT(*) OVER group(comments.PostId) (implemented as COUNT(*) in GROUP BY comments.PostId) | comment_avg_score = AVG(comments.Score) OVER group(comments.PostId) (implemented as AVG(Score) in GROUP BY comments.PostId) | first_comment_date = MIN(comments.CreationDate) OVER group(comments.PostId) (implemented as MIN(CreationDate) in GROUP BY comments.PostId) | last_comment_date = MAX(comments.CreationDate) OVER group(comments.PostId) (implemented as MAX(CreationDate) in GROUP BY comments.PostId)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic (NORM) on comments_per_post_agg.PostId = posts_basic.Id — safe because posts_basic has one row per post (this view is one-row-per-PostId so measures are not duplicated). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner (JOIN) on comments_per_post_agg.PostId = posts_with_owner.Id — safe if posts_with_owner is one-row-per-post (do not join if posts_with_owner contains multiple owner-related duplicates for the same post). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to votes_per_post_agg (AGG) on PostId — safe because both are aggregated to one row per PostId, so combining metrics (e.g., comment_count + vote_count) is safe. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_badge_counts (AGG) only when joining via the post owner id (posts_with_owner -> owner user id) after resolving to one row per post; do not directly join comments_per_post_agg to user_badge_counts on PostId (different grain). | do NOT join without re-aggregation to any one-to-many relation keyed to PostId such as postlinks_edges (JOIN) or latest_posthistory_per_post (RANK) if those views can return multiple rows per PostId — such joins will multiply comment_count and distort AVG and min/max unless you first aggregate the multiplicative side to one row per PostId or re-compute measures appropriately. | do NOT join directly to tag lists or post-tags multi-row tables (e.g., tags lookup relationships) on PostId without aggregating tags to one row per PostId first, because that will duplicate counts and change averages. | safe composition pattern: (comments_per_post_agg JOIN posts_basic ON PostId) LEFT JOIN votes_per_post_agg USING (PostId) — all three sides are one-row-per-post so measures remain correct. | safe composition pattern for roll-up: if you need site-wide aggregates that combine comment_count with another one-to-many detail, SUM(comment_count) after joining to a deduplicated set of posts (one row per PostId) or join only to other per-post aggregates.

views.description: Aggregated comment-level measures per post: comment count, average comment score, first and last comment dates. Use this to enrich post-level analytics without joining raw comments. | Use for: Find posts with many comments or long discussion windows; Join to posts to compare post CommentCount metadata versus actual comment rows; Identify posts whose comments are declining/increasing in score

views.name: votes_per_post_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PostId,
  SUM(CASE WHEN VoteTypeId IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS votes_total,
  SUM(CASE WHEN VoteTypeId = VoteTypeId THEN 0 END) AS votes_placeholder
FROM votes
GROUP BY PostId

params.description: Per-post aggregated vote counts (one row per PostId) — total votes and a placeholder metric.
params.when_to_use: Get the total number of votes for a given post or set of posts | Filter or rank posts by their vote totals (e.g., top-voted posts) | Join vote totals onto post-level queries when you need one row per post | Compose into larger aggregates by joining on PostId (careful about join cardinality)
params.output_schema: PostId: identifier of the post (GROUP BY key) — derived from votes.PostId | votes_total: integer count of rows in votes for this PostId where VoteTypeId IS NOT NULL — derived from SUM(CASE WHEN VoteTypeId IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over votes.VoteTypeId | votes_placeholder: numeric result of SUM(CASE WHEN VoteTypeId = VoteTypeId THEN 0 END) — derived from the same votes.VoteTypeId expression in the SELECT (this expression always yields 0 per row and so the aggregate is effectively 0 for each PostId)
params.metric: votes_total = SUM(CASE WHEN votes.VoteTypeId IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) GROUP BY votes.PostId | votes_placeholder = SUM(CASE WHEN votes.VoteTypeId = votes.VoteTypeId THEN 0 END) GROUP BY votes.PostId  -- deterministic 0 per PostId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic (NORM) on posts_basic.Id = votes_per_post_agg.PostId — safe because votes_per_post_agg has exactly one row per PostId, so joining will attach vote measures to each post without duplication. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner (JOIN) on posts_with_owner.Id = votes_per_post_agg.PostId — safe for the same reason as posts_basic; posts_with_owner is one-row-per-post. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup (NORM) on tags_lookup.TagId = <some_tag_id> only when tags_lookup is being used as a dimension lookup that remains one-row-per-key; joining tags to posts typically requires a many-to-many handling (see unsafe guidance). | DO NOT join directly to comments_per_post_agg (AGG) on PostId without care if you plan to re-aggregate: comments_per_post_agg is also one-row-per-PostId and joining it to this view is safe for combining per-post aggregates (e.g., SELECT ... FROM votes_per_post_agg v JOIN comments_per_post_agg c USING (PostId)). However, if you instead join to a non-aggregated comments or postlinks_edges table that has multiple rows per PostId, you will multiply votes_total unless you re-aggregate after the join. | DO NOT join to one-to-many tables/views such as postlinks_edges (JOIN) or any raw comments table (not the aggregated comments_per_post_agg) without re-aggregation: those joins will duplicate the votes_total measure because votes_per_post_agg is one-row-per-PostId but the other side may have many rows per PostId. | When composing into larger metrics (e.g., total votes across a set of posts after joining to a tags or users dimension), prefer either: (a) join this view to one-row-per-post dimensions and then SUM(votes_total) at the outer query, or (b) if joining to many-rows-per-post, perform the aggregation on votes_per_post_agg before the join (e.g., keep it as a derived table keyed by PostId) and aggregate only after deduplication. | Example safe pattern: SELECT p.OwnerUserId, SUM(v.votes_total) FROM posts_basic p JOIN votes_per_post_agg v ON p.Id = v.PostId GROUP BY p.OwnerUserId — safe because both sides are one-row-per-post and the SUM aggregates per owner. | Example unsafe pattern: SELECT p.Id, v.votes_total, pl.LinkId FROM votes_per_post_agg v JOIN postlinks_edges pl ON pl.PostId = v.PostId — unsafe if postlinks_edges has multiple edges per PostId and you expect votes_total to remain a correct per-row measure; it will be duplicated for each matching edge. To use, either aggregate after join or join to a deduplicated postlinks_edges (one-row-per-PostId) first.

views.description: Aggregated vote counts per post broken out by VoteTypeId. Produces counts per (PostId, VoteTypeId) and a pivot-friendly wide summary (one row per PostId) with total votes. Use for vote-type specific analyses and to compare against posts.Score. | Use for: Compare recorded votes events to post Score or to detect missing aggregations; Break down votes by VoteTypeId when expanded downstream (this CTE provides total count; callers can re-aggregate by VoteTypeId if needed)

views.name: user_badge_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count,
  MIN(Date) AS first_badge_date,
  MAX(Date) AS last_badge_date
FROM badges
GROUP BY UserId

params.description: Per-user aggregates of badge activity: total badges and first/last badge dates per user.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of badges a given user has received | Filter or rank users by how many badges they have | Combine a user's badge activity (count, first/last badge dates) with other per-user attributes | Compose into queries that need a single-row-per-user badge summary as input for further aggregation or joins
params.output_schema: UserId: the identifier of the user (sourced from badges.UserId) | badge_count: COUNT(*) of rows in badges for that UserId — total number of badge records the user has (derived from COUNT(*) over badges grouped by UserId) | first_badge_date: the earliest badges.Date for that UserId (derived from MIN(Date) over badges grouped by UserId) | last_badge_date: the latest badges.Date for that UserId (derived from MAX(Date) over badges grouped by UserId)
params.metric: badge_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of badge rows per badges.UserId (aggregate computed from badges table) | first_badge_date = MIN(badges.Date)  -- earliest badge Date per badges.UserId | last_badge_date = MAX(badges.Date)  -- latest badge Date per badges.UserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user-level (one-row-per-user) dimensions or views on UserId — safe to join to posts_with_owner on posts_with_owner.UserId = user_badge_counts.UserId because posts_with_owner is one row per post but represents a many side; however, joining this AGG (one row per user) to a one-row-per-user users table or normalized user view is safe because user_badge_counts is already one-row-per-UserId so its measures will not be duplicated. | safe: join to a users dimension (if present) on UserId — safe because that dimension is one-row-per-user, so badge_count and date metrics remain correct. | safe: use in further aggregation keyed by UserId (for example, SELECT u.UserId, ubc.badge_count FROM user_badge_counts ubc JOIN users u USING (UserId)) — safe because the join is 1:1. | do NOT naively join to one-to-many tables/views (e.g., posts_basic, comments_per_post_agg (per post), votes_per_post_agg (per post), postlinks_edges, latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank) on UserId without re-aggregation because those joins will multiply rows per user and therefore duplicate badge_count and distort first/last dates. Instead, either: | - join to a per-user aggregation of those one-to-many tables (aggregate posts/comments/votes by UserId first), or | - join this view as the preserved one-row-per-user side and aggregate the multiplied result back to user level (e.g., SUM(ubc.badge_count) after grouping by UserId is unnecessary; instead re-compute aggregates from the multiplied join correctly), or | - use lateral/subquery (e.g., EXISTS or separate aggregated subqueries) so badge_count is not multiplied. | example safe composition patterns: | - Enrich user rows: SELECT u.UserId, u.Name, ubc.badge_count FROM users u LEFT JOIN user_badge_counts ubc ON u.UserId = ubc.UserId  -- safe (1:1 or 1:0-1) | - Combine with per-post aggregates: if you need badge_count alongside per-user post_count, first compute posts_per_user = (SELECT OwnerUserId, COUNT(*) AS post_count FROM posts_basic GROUP BY OwnerUserId) then join posts_per_user to user_badge_counts on posts_per_user.OwnerUserId = user_badge_counts.UserId — safe because both sides are one-row-per-user after aggregation. | rationale: this view's grain is one row per badges.UserId. Any join that preserves that 1-row-per-user cardinality (1:1 or many:1 where this view is on the 1 side) will not duplicate the measures. Joining to tables where the other side has many rows per UserId without first aggregating will multiply badge_count and make first_badge_date/last_badge_date ambiguous unless you re-aggregate or apply appropriate window/ DISTINCT logic.

views.description: Badge counts per user and date of first/last badge. Useful for measuring user recognition and activity milestones. | Use for: Rank users by total badges or recent badge activity; Filter users with no badges or with badges within a time window

views.name: latest_posthistory_per_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostHistoryTypeId,
  PostId,
  RevisionGUID,
  CreationDate,
  UserId,
  Text,
  Comment,
  UserDisplayName,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY PostId ORDER BY CreationDate DESC, Id DESC) AS rev_rank
FROM postHistory

semantic_filters.PostId: NULL (grouping key; no fixed literal filter)

params.description: Provides the latest (most recent) post-history entry per post, with rank (rev_rank) indicating recency within each PostId.
params.when_to_use: Get the most recent edit/change metadata for a specific post (e.g., latest revision text, who edited, when). | Filter to latest revision per post (rev_rank = 1) and join to post-level data to show current displayed content or recent edit info. | Compose time-ordered revision history queries where you need to identify or label the latest revision among many per post. | Build aggregates or filters that depend on the most-recent revision (e.g., count posts whose latest revision contains a keyword).
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of this postHistory row (derived from base column postHistory.Id) | PostHistoryTypeId: type code for this post history entry (derived from postHistory.PostHistoryTypeId) | PostId: identifier of the post this history row belongs to (derived from postHistory.PostId) | RevisionGUID: GUID for this revision (derived from postHistory.RevisionGUID) | CreationDate: timestamp when this history row was created; used to determine recency (derived from postHistory.CreationDate) | UserId: user identifier who made the change (derived from postHistory.UserId) | Text: textual content of this revision entry (derived from postHistory.Text) | Comment: edit/comment string for this history entry (derived from postHistory.Comment) | UserDisplayName: display name captured on the history row (derived from postHistory.UserDisplayName) | rev_rank: rank within each PostId ordered by CreationDate DESC, Id DESC (derived by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY PostId ORDER BY CreationDate DESC, Id DESC))
params.grounded_columns: postHistory.Id | postHistory.PostHistoryTypeId | postHistory.PostId | postHistory.RevisionGUID | postHistory.CreationDate | postHistory.UserId | postHistory.Text | postHistory.Comment | postHistory.UserDisplayName
params.metric: rev_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY postHistory.PostId ORDER BY postHistory.CreationDate DESC, postHistory.Id DESC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic on posts_basic.Id = latest_posthistory_per_post.PostId — safe because latest_posthistory_per_post is at most one row per PostId when you filter to rev_rank = 1, so measures from posts_basic will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner on posts_with_owner.Id = latest_posthistory_per_post.PostId — safe only after restricting to rev_rank = 1. Without that restriction, latest_posthistory_per_post can have many rows per PostId and would duplicate post-level data. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup via posts_basic -> posts_basic.Id = tags_lookup.PostId is NOT safe directly from this view unless you aggregate tags_lookup first (e.g., group tags per post) because tags_lookup is one-to-many per post and would multiply rows/measures. Instead, aggregate tags by PostId (e.g., array_agg or count) before joining. | do NOT join directly to comments_per_post_agg on PostId without care: comments_per_post_agg is already aggregated per post (AGG) and is safe to join on PostId because it is one-row-per-post. If you instead join to a raw comments table (not present in sibling views), that would multiply rows. | do NOT join directly to votes_per_post_agg on PostId is safe because votes_per_post_agg is aggregated per post (one-row-per-post). If you join to a non-aggregated votes table, you would duplicate latest_posthistory_per_post rows. | do NOT join to user_badge_counts (aggregated per user) on UserId is safe — user_badge_counts is AGG per user, so it will not multiply latest-post rows when joined on UserId. | when joining to rank or edge sibling views (e.g., top_posts_by_score_rank or postlinks_edges), ensure you understand those view grains: top_posts_by_score_rank is rank-per-post (may be one row per post) so joining on PostId is safe; postlinks_edges (JOIN) may be many-to-many (post->linked post) and will multiply rows and must be pre-aggregated or used in a subquery that restricts to one row per PostId. | general rule: latest_posthistory_per_post is RANKed over postHistory and produces potentially many rows per PostId (one per history row) unless you filter to rev_rank = 1. To preserve cardinality and avoid duplicating measures, always either (a) filter this view to rev_rank = 1 before joining to one-row-per-post dimensions, or (b) join only to other aggregated/one-row-per-key views (comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, user_badge_counts, posts_basic) on the matching key. Do not join to one-to-many detail tables (raw postHistory, tags lookup if multiple tags per post, postlinks_edges raw edges) without re-aggregating or otherwise preventing row multiplication.

views.description: Latest postHistory row per PostId based on CreationDate. Exposes revision metadata and a rank so callers can restrict to the latest or inspect recent revisions. | Use for: Select latest revision per post, audit most recent editor activity, join to posts to show latest revision text; Find posts with frequent edits by counting ranks or filtering rev_rank = 1

views.name: top_posts_by_score_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  CreaionDate,
  Score,
  Title,
  OwnerUserId,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(CreaionDate) ORDER BY Score DESC, ViewCount DESC, Id ASC) AS daily_score_rank
FROM posts

params.description: Ranks posts by Score per calendar day, returning one row per post with its daily score rank.
params.when_to_use: Find the top N posts for a given date or date range by score (e.g., daily leaderboards). | Filter or join to select posts whose daily_score_rank is within a threshold (e.g., top 10 posts each day). | Compose additional aggregations or metrics that need a per-post daily rank (for reporting or downstream ranking-based filters). | As a base for time-partitioned analytics where ranking within each day is required before joining to other entities.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the post, derived from posts.Id | CreaionDate: creation timestamp/date of the post, derived from posts.CreaionDate | Score: integer score of the post, derived from posts.Score | Title: title text of the post, derived from posts.Title | OwnerUserId: user id of the post owner, derived from posts.OwnerUserId | daily_score_rank: integer rank of the post within the calendar date of CreaionDate, computed by RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(CreaionDate) ORDER BY Score DESC, ViewCount DESC, Id ASC)
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.CreaionDate | posts.Score | posts.Title | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.ViewCount
params.metric: daily_score_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DATE(posts.CreaionDate) ORDER BY posts.Score DESC, posts.ViewCount DESC, posts.Id ASC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic (NORM) on Id — safe because posts_basic is one-row-per-post (same grain as this view), so joining preserves row-level uniqueness and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner (JOIN) on Id — safe when posts_with_owner is a 1:1 enrichment of posts (same grain), so daily_score_rank remains unduplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup on tag Ids via an intermediate 1:1 post->tag mapping that has been aggregated to one row per post (e.g., a concatenated tag list) — safe only if the tag side has been reduced to one row per post beforehand; otherwise it will multiply rows. | DO NOT join directly to comments_per_post_agg (AGG) without matching on Id — joining on Id is safe because comments_per_post_agg is an aggregate per post (one row per post). If comments_per_post_agg is per post, join on Id is safe; if it were per-post-per-something, it would not be safe. | DO NOT join directly to votes_per_post_agg (AGG) or user_badge_counts (AGG) without verifying those aggregates are one-row-per-post (for votes_per_post_agg) or one-row-per-user (for user_badge_counts). Specifically: | - votes_per_post_agg: safe to join on Id if that view is aggregated to one row per post (it should be); otherwise it will multiply rows. | - user_badge_counts: safe to join on OwnerUserId if user_badge_counts is one-row-per-user (aggregate). That join will not duplicate this view's measures because it maps many posts to one user. | DO NOT join directly to postlinks_edges or tags/details where the target is many-to-many (e.g., post -> multiple linked posts or post -> multiple tags) without first aggregating the many-side to one row per post (e.g., count of links, concatenated tags). Joining a one-to-many child will multiply rows and thus duplicate the daily_score_rank measure. | When composing metrics that aggregate over this view (for example, count of top-10 posts per day, average score of top-10), perform the aggregation after applying the rank filter (e.g., WHERE daily_score_rank <= 10) to avoid duplicating row counts. | If you need to join to latest_posthistory_per_post (RANK): ensure latest_posthistory_per_post is one-row-per-post (it is expected to be a rank-per-post windowed to latest); joining on Id is safe and will not duplicate rows if that sibling view has been reduced to one row per post. | General rule: safe joins = joins to views/tables that are at the same grain (one row per posts.Id) or to true dimensions that are one-row-per-key (e.g., user by OwnerUserId). Unsafe joins = joining to one-to-many children (comments, tags, links) without pre-aggregation, because they will multiply rows and thus duplicate this view's per-post measures.

views.description: Per-day rank of posts by Score within each CreaionDate date. Exposes a dense_rank-like column so callers can select top-K per day. Useful for time-windowed top-post queries. | Use for: Get top-N scored posts per day by filtering daily_score_rank <= N downstream, compare daily top posts over time; Combine with posts_with_owner to show owner attributes for top posts

views.name: postlinks_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  CreationDate,
  PostId,
  RelatedPostId,
  LinkTypeId
FROM postLinks

params.description: One-row-per-post-link listing of links between posts (id, creation time, source post, related post, and link type).
params.when_to_use: Find links from or to a specific post (e.g., get all related posts for PostId = X). | Filter links by creation date or link type (e.g., links created in a date range or of a particular LinkTypeId). | Compose post-level analyses that need the existence or identity of a link (e.g., count links per post when aggregated). | Serve as a stable one-row-per-link detail input to joins that enrich link rows with post or user attributes before aggregation.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the postLinks row (derived from postLinks.Id) | CreationDate: timestamp when the link was created (derived from postLinks.CreationDate) | PostId: the source post id (the post that has the link) (derived from postLinks.PostId) | RelatedPostId: the target/related post id (derived from postLinks.RelatedPostId) | LinkTypeId: numeric code representing the type of link (derived from postLinks.LinkTypeId)
params.metric: Id = identity(postLinks.Id) | CreationDate = identity(postLinks.CreationDate) | PostId = identity(postLinks.PostId) | RelatedPostId = identity(postLinks.RelatedPostId) | LinkTypeId = identity(postLinks.LinkTypeId) | row_count_of_links = count(postLinks.Id)  -- can be computed by aggregating Id if a metric is needed
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic on postlinks_edges.PostId = posts_basic.Id — safe because posts_basic is one-row-per-post, so joining enriches each link with its source post attributes without duplicating link rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic on postlinks_edges.RelatedPostId = posts_basic.Id — safe for the same reason when enriching the related/target post. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner on postlinks_edges.PostId = posts_with_owner.Id — safe because posts_with_owner is one-row-per-post (JOIN), so it will not multiply postlink rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup only after joining to a post dimension that is one-row-per-post and then aggregating tags per-post, or join tags_lookup to posts_basic first. Do not directly join postlinks_edges to tags_lookup on PostId = Tag.PostId if tags_lookup is many-to-many (tags per post) because it will multiply link rows. | DO NOT join postlinks_edges directly to any one-to-many aggregate/detail views such as comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, user_badge_counts, latest_posthistory_per_post, or top_posts_by_score_rank if those views are many-rows-per-post without re-aggregation — joining to a many-side will multiply link rows. Instead, either: | - aggregate postlinks_edges after joining (e.g., count links per PostId) or | - pre-aggregate the many-side to one-row-per-post (or per-key) before joining, or | - join to a one-row-per-post view (posts_basic or posts_with_owner) and then join the aggregated metrics. | Examples of safe composition patterns: | - To get number of links per post: SELECT p.Id, COUNT(l.Id) FROM posts_basic p LEFT JOIN postlinks_edges l ON l.PostId = p.Id GROUP BY p.Id — safe because aggregation is applied after the one-to-many join. | - To enrich each link with source and target post titles: SELECT l.*, src.Title AS SourceTitle, tgt.Title AS TargetTitle FROM postlinks_edges l LEFT JOIN posts_basic src ON src.Id = l.PostId LEFT JOIN posts_basic tgt ON tgt.Id = l.RelatedPostId — safe because both posts_basic joins are one-to-one (one-row-per-post). | Rationale: postlinks_edges is one-row-per-link (grain = ['Id']). Joining to one-row-per-post dimensions keyed by PostId or RelatedPostId will not duplicate measures. Joining directly to one-to-many tables keyed by PostId (e.g., tags, comments) will duplicate link rows unless the many-side is first aggregated to one-row-per-post or the query re-aggregates after joining.

views.description: Simple edge list for post links preserving direction and link type. One row per link (PostId -> RelatedPostId) with creation date for temporal analyses of linking behavior. | Use for: Analyze duplicate or related posts by following edges, build graphs of post relationships, join to posts to get titles for linked posts

views.name: tags_lookup
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  TagName,
  Count,
  ExcerptPostId,
  WikiPostId
FROM tags

params.description: Provides one row per tag with its name and basic metadata (count and related post IDs).
params.when_to_use: List tags with their total usage count (Count) and associated excerpt/wiki post IDs. | Filter or look up a tag by Id to join tag metadata into higher-level analyses (for example, annotate posts with their tag names by joining through a tag-post linking table). | Compose into aggregations by tag (e.g., sum metrics of posts grouped by tag) when the tag identity and its static metadata are needed.
params.output_schema: Id: the tag primary identifier from tags.Id | TagName: the human-readable tag text from tags.TagName | Count: the integer usage count (how many times the tag has been applied) from tags.Count | ExcerptPostId: the posts.Id of the excerpt (synopsis) post for the tag from tags.ExcerptPostId | WikiPostId: the posts.Id of the tag wiki post for the tag from tags.WikiPostId
params.metric: Count = tags.Count (base column; not an aggregate in this view)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to post-level or user-level dimension views that are one-row-per-key on the matching key — safe examples: |   - join to posts_basic on posts_basic.Id = tags.ExcerptPostId — safe because posts_basic is one-row-per-post and this view is one-row-per-tag, so tag rows will not be multiplicatively duplicated when bringing in excerpt post columns. |   - join to posts_basic on posts_basic.Id = tags.WikiPostId — safe for the same reason as above. |   - join to posts_with_owner on posts_with_owner.Id = tags.ExcerptPostId or tags.WikiPostId — safe because posts_with_owner is one-row-per-post (JOIN) and will not duplicate tag-level measures. |  | do NOT join directly (without re-aggregation) to one-to-many aggregation or event-level views/tables that can multiply tag rows, for example: |   - do NOT join to comments_per_post_agg or votes_per_post_agg on a post key expecting counts to remain unchanged unless you aggregate/limit first, because those are one-row-per-post aggregates only if joined on the exact post key; joining them via a postless many-to-many link could duplicate rows. |   - do NOT join to postlinks_edges (a join/edge view) or any other one-to-many relationship table that links tags to many posts without first ensuring a one-row-per-(tag,post) or re-aggregating, because such joins can multiply the tag rows and thus duplicate tag-level measures like Count. |  | recommended safe composition patterns: |   - To enrich tag rows with excerpt/wiki post fields: LEFT JOIN posts_basic ON posts_basic.Id = tags.ExcerptPostId (or tags.WikiPostId). This preserves one-row-per-tag. |   - To compute metrics derived from posts that use a tag, first build or use an aggregated mapping from tag.Id to the desired metric (one-row-per-tag), then join that aggregated result to this view on tags.Id. This prevents duplication of tag-level measures. |  | explanatory note on duplication: this view's measures are the per-tag base columns from the tags table (one row per tags.Id). Joining it to another dataset that has multiple rows per tag (for example, a post-tag mapping with many posts per tag) will multiply tag rows; therefore, such joins must be accompanied by join-to-aggregates or grouping on the consuming side to keep counts/metrics correct.

views.description: Tag master list with tag metadata. Use this to join tag definitions to parsed post tag tokens downstream. | Use for: Map post tag tokens to tag metadata, find popular tags, enrich posts by tag definitions

views.name: users_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  Reputation AS Reputation,
  Id AS Id
FROM users

params.description: A normalized user core view giving one row per user with the user's display name, reputation, and user id.
params.when_to_use: Lookup user attributes (display name, reputation) by user id | Join user attributes into post/comment-level or aggregate queries while preserving one-row-per-user semantics | Use as a dimension table when aggregating metrics by user
params.output_schema: DisplayName: the user's display name as taken directly from users.DisplayName | Reputation: the user's reputation score as taken directly from users.Reputation | Id: the user's primary key id as taken directly from users.Id
params.metric: DisplayName = users.DisplayName | Reputation = users.Reputation | Id = users.Id
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic (or posts_with_owner) on posts.owner_user_id = users_core.Id — safe when posts_basic is used as the many side and users_core is the one side because users_core has one row per Id, so joining users_core to post rows will not duplicate user rows (it will replicate user attributes across post rows which is intended). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_badge_counts on user_badge_counts.UserId = users_core.Id — safe because user_badge_counts is an aggregated one-row-per-user (AGG) view; joining preserves one row per user and does not multiply metrics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to comments_per_post_agg only after ensuring the join key is to a post-level or aggregated-by-user result. Do NOT directly join users_core to comments_per_post_agg on comments_per_post_agg.PostId = users_core.Id because that is a mismatched key (post vs user) and would produce incorrect multiplicative joins. | do NOT join users_core to one-to-many tables/views (for example, raw posts, comments, votes_per_post_agg if it is aggregated by post) and expect user-level measures to remain unchanged unless you aggregate the one-to-many side first. Example unsafe join: users_core JOIN posts_basic ON users_core.Id = posts_basic.OwnerUserId and then selecting user-level metrics without aggregating posts_basic will produce one row per post and thus multiply user-level counts/measures. | safe composition pattern: when you need user-level metrics combined with many-side data, first aggregate the many-side to one row per user (for example, COUNT(posts) AS NumPosts grouped by OwnerUserId in posts_basic or use user_badge_counts), then join that aggregate to users_core on Id — this prevents duplication of user rows or double-counting. | safe join to sibling normalized lookups like tags_lookup only when keys match and semantics are one-to-one; do NOT join to rank or edge views (latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank, postlinks_edges) without verifying they are aggregated to the same grain or re-aggregating, because those are per-post or per-edge and will multiply rows relative to users_core.

views.description: A normalized user core view giving one row per user with the user's display name, reputation, and user id.
validated_on: What is the average score of the posts owned by the user csgillespie?

views.name: posts_by_owner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(Id) AS post_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN PostTypeId = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS answer_count_sum,
  SUM(CASE WHEN PostTypeId = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS question_count
FROM posts
WHERE OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY OwnerUserId

params.description: Per-owner (OwnerUserId) aggregate counts of posts, answers, and questions — useful for summarizing a user's post activity.
params.when_to_use: Get total posts, answers, and questions for a specific user or set of users | Join user-level post activity into user summaries or profiles | Compute rates or ratios per user (e.g., answers/posts) by joining to user demographic or time-bucketed data | Filter or rank users by their post/activity volume before further analysis
params.output_schema: OwnerUserId: the owner user's identifier (derived from posts.OwnerUserId) | post_count: COUNT(Id) — total number of posts by this OwnerUserId (derived from COUNT(posts.Id)) | answer_count_sum: SUM(CASE WHEN PostTypeId = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) — total number of posts by this OwnerUserId that are answers (derived from posts.PostTypeId) | question_count: SUM(CASE WHEN PostTypeId = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) — total number of posts by this OwnerUserId that are questions (derived from posts.PostTypeId)
params.metric: post_count = COUNT(posts.Id)  -- count of rows in posts per OwnerUserId (NULL OwnerUserId excluded by WHERE clause) | answer_count_sum = SUM(CASE WHEN posts.PostTypeId = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of answer-type posts per OwnerUserId | question_count = SUM(CASE WHEN posts.PostTypeId = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of question-type posts per OwnerUserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because posts_by_owner has one row per OwnerUserId, so joining to the one-row-per-user users_core will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_badge_counts on OwnerUserId = user_badge_counts.UserId — safe if user_badge_counts is one-row-per-user (it is an AGG); the posts_by_owner measures will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup on OwnerUserId = tags_lookup.Id is NOT appropriate — tags_lookup is a normalization of tags (not keyed by OwnerUserId), do not join on mismatched keys. | do NOT join directly to posts_basic, posts_with_owner, latest_posthistory_per_post, comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, postlinks_edges, or top_posts_by_score_rank without re-aggregating because those are either one-to-many with respect to OwnerUserId (per-post, per-comment, per-vote, per-postlink, or ranked per-post outputs) and will multiply posts_by_owner's measures. Instead, aggregate the child relation to OwnerUserId first (e.g., sum comment counts per OwnerUserId) or join on post-level and re-aggregate: | safe composition pattern: to combine per-owner post_count with per-post metrics (e.g., votes_per_post_agg), first aggregate the per-post metric to OwnerUserId by joining posts (Id, OwnerUserId) to votes_per_post_agg on post id and then GROUP BY OwnerUserId — this prevents double-counting. | safe composition pattern: when joining any one-to-many child (comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank, postlinks_edges), perform aggregation to OwnerUserId or use DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER to reduce to one row per OwnerUserId before joining to posts_by_owner. | summary rule: you may freely join posts_by_owner to any dimension that is one-row-per-user (users_core, user_badge_counts if aggregated by user) without re-aggregation; you must not join it to tables or views that are many-rows-per-OwnerUserId (per-post, per-comment, per-vote, per-link) unless those are re-aggregated to OwnerUserId first because such joins will multiply and corrupt post_count, answer_count_sum, and question_count.

views.description: Per-owner (OwnerUserId) aggregate counts of posts, answers, and questions — useful for summarizing a user's post activity.

views.name: badges_by_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count,
  MAX(Date) AS latest_badge_date
FROM badges
GROUP BY UserId

params.description: Per-user aggregate of badges: count of badges and most recent badge date for each user.
params.when_to_use: Get how many badges a specific user has and when they last received a badge. | Rank or filter users by badge count or by recency of badge. | Join badge summary to user-level queries (e.g., user profile, activity summaries) without re-aggregating badge details. | Compose higher-level analytics that need one-row-per-user badge metrics (e.g., correlation of badge_count with post counts).
params.output_schema: UserId: identifier for the user; derived from badges.UserId (grouping key) | badge_count: integer count of badge rows for that UserId; derived from COUNT(*) over badges rows | latest_badge_date: latest badge Date for that UserId; derived from MAX(Date) over badges.Date
params.metric: badge_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of rows in badges partitioned by badges.UserId | latest_badge_date = MAX(badges.Date)  -- greatest Date value in badges partitioned by badges.UserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to users_core on users_core.Id = badges_by_user.UserId — safe because badges_by_user is one row per UserId so its measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE: join to posts_by_owner on posts_by_owner.UserId = badges_by_user.UserId — safe when posts_by_owner is itself one-row-per-user (it is an AGG with grain ['UserId']). | cardinality-SAFE: join to user_badge_counts on user_badge_counts.UserId = badges_by_user.UserId — safe if the sibling view is one-row-per-user (do not join if sibling is multi-row per user). | DO NOT join directly to posts_basic or posts_with_owner (both can be many rows per user) without re-aggregation: joining badges_by_user to a one-to-many posts table will duplicate badge_count and distort counts/metrics. If you need combined metrics, either (a) aggregate posts to one row per UserId first (e.g., posts_by_owner) then join, or (b) join and then re-aggregate over UserId in the final query. | DO NOT join directly to comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank, postlinks_edges, or any post/comment-level RANK/JOIN views that are many-rows-per-user, unless you plan to re-aggregate after the join. Those are many-to-one relative to UserId and would multiply badge_count. | SAFE to use as a building block in analytic compositions that expect user-level metrics: treat badge_count and latest_badge_date as user-level measures that should be combined with other user-level aggregates (one-row-per-user) to avoid double-counting. | If you must join to a child (many) relation for detailed analysis (for example, attach each badge row), join back to the base badges table on badges.UserId = badges_by_user.UserId — but be aware this will expand rows; then re-aggregate if you need user-level results.

views.description: Per-user aggregate of badges: count of badges and most recent badge date for each user.

views.name: users_core_12
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  DisplayName,
  CreationDate,
  Reputation,
  AccountId
FROM users

params.description: Basic user-level attributes for each user.Id (display name, creation date, reputation, and linked account id).
params.when_to_use: Look up profile attributes for a specific user by Id. | Filter or join users as a driving set before composing aggregates about that user's posts, comments, badges, or votes. | Include user identity attributes in analytics (e.g., list top users, cohort by creation date) without changing row cardinality.
params.output_schema: Id: the user's unique identifier — derived directly from users.Id | DisplayName: the user's display name — derived directly from users.DisplayName | CreationDate: timestamp when the user account was created — derived directly from users.CreationDate | Reputation: current reputation score for the user — derived directly from users.Reputation | AccountId: associated network account identifier (nullable) — derived directly from users.AccountId

GROUP BY posts_rowlevel.Id) | When joining to aggregation siblings (comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg): join on posts_rowlevel.Id = comments_per_post_agg.PostId (or votes_per_post_agg.PostId).
