These views are post- or post-related and are many-to-one relative to users; joining them directly without re-aggregation will multiply user rows. | do NOT join directly to posts_with_owner, comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, postlinks_edges, or tags_lookup (where the relation is many posts/comments/votes → one user) without re-aggregating the many-side first, because users_rowlevel is 1 row per user and a raw many-side join will duplicate the user row and thus multiply any user-level measures (e.g., Reputation) incorrectly. | When composing metrics per user: if you join a one-to-many child (posts, comments, votes) to users_rowlevel, either (a) aggregate the child to one row per user first (e.g., count of posts per OwnerUserId), then join, or (b) join and then group by users_rowlevel.Id and re-compute aggregates (COUNT, SUM) to avoid duplication. | Examples of safe patterns: (1) users_rowlevel JOIN posts_by_owner ON Id = OwnerUserId — safe because posts_by_owner is already aggregated by OwnerUserId. (2) users_rowlevel LEFT JOIN (SELECT OwnerUserId, COUNT(*) AS post_count FROM posts GROUP BY OwnerUserId) p ON users_rowlevel.Id = p.OwnerUserId — safe because child was aggregated before join. | Examples of unsafe patterns: users_rowlevel JOIN posts ON users_rowlevel.Id = posts.OwnerUserId without subsequent GROUP BY users_rowlevel.Id will produce multiple rows per user and will duplicate user-level measures.

views.description: One row per user with basic user attributes (Id, DisplayName, Reputation, CreationDate); answers questions about user identity and user-level attributes.

views.name: post_owner_user_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title",
  posts.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId",
  users.DisplayName AS "users.DisplayName",
  users.Reputation AS "users.Reputation"
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id

params.description: Provides post rows along with the display name and reputation of the post owner (if any).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve posts together with their owner's public profile fields (DisplayName, Reputation). | Filter, sort, or page posts while showing owner name/reputation without additional joins. | Compose higher-level aggregations or metrics about posts that need owner attributes as dimensions (e.g., posts by owner reputation band). | Use as a building block when joining additional one-row-per-post or one-row-per-user entities in a cardinality-safe way (see composition guidance).
params.output_schema: posts.Id: the primary identifier of the post, derived from posts.Id | posts.Title: the title text of the post, derived from posts.Title | posts.OwnerUserId: foreign key referencing the owning user, derived from posts.OwnerUserId | users.DisplayName: the owner's display name (nullable if OwnerUserId is null or no matching user), derived from users.DisplayName | users.Reputation: the owner's reputation score (nullable if OwnerUserId is null or no matching user), derived from users.Reputation
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.Title | posts.OwnerUserId | users.Id | users.DisplayName | users.Reputation
params.metric: No aggregate metrics are defined in this view. All output columns are direct projections: posts.Id = posts.Id, posts.Title = posts.Title, posts.OwnerUserId = posts.OwnerUserId, users.DisplayName = users.DisplayName, users.Reputation = users.Reputation
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (or any one-row-per-user view) on posts.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because posts.OwnerUserId maps each post to at most one user row, so this view remains one-row-per-post and its columns are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_posthistory_per_post (RANK) on posts.Id = latest_posthistory_per_post.PostId — safe because latest_posthistory_per_post is one-row-per-post (ranked selection), preserving one-row-per-post cardinality. | DO NOT join directly to posts_by_owner (AGG) on posts.OwnerUserId = posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId without re-aggregating or ensuring key uniqueness — posts_by_owner is an aggregate with one-row-per-owner; joining it to this per-post view is safe only if you intend to denormalize owner-level aggregates onto each post (it will duplicate owner-level metrics per post but that duplication is intentional). If you want to preserve post-level grain, prefer joining to posts_by_owner only when you understand the aggregation semantics. | DO NOT join to one-to-many detail tables or aggregates that are one-to-many with respect to posts (for example comments_per_post_agg is one-row-per-post so safe; however joining to a raw comments table or any view that is one-to-many per post would multiply rows) without first aggregating those details to one-row-per-post. Specifically, avoid joining to raw comments (one-to-many) on posts.Id unless you aggregate comments (e.g., comments_per_post_agg) to avoid multiplying post rows and duplicating post-level attributes. | When composing higher-level aggregates (for example computing total comments by owner using this view), ensure you aggregate at the desired grain after joins: if you join this view to comments_per_post_agg (one-row-per-post), the join is one-to-one on posts.Id and safe. If you join to votes_per_post_agg (one-row-per-post), it's also one-to-one and safe. | If you need to join to tags_lookup or other tag lookup tables that are one-to-many per post (post ↔ tag), first use an aggregate (e.g., tag counts per post) before joining to this view to avoid multiplying posts. | Summary rule: this view is one-row-per-post (grain: posts.Id). Safe joins are those that are one-row-per-post or one-row-per-user where the intended effect is to enrich each post by its owner; avoid or pre-aggregate joins to any table/view that is many-per-post unless you accept or control row multiplication by re-aggregating afterwards.

views.description: Provides post rows along with the display name and reputation of the post owner (if any).

views.name: posts_core_52
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id,
  p.Title,
  p.OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(p.OwnerDisplayName, u.DisplayName) AS OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id

params.description: Provides one-row-per-post core attributes: Id, Title, OwnerUserId and a resolved OwnerDisplayName (post's stored name or the user's DisplayName).
params.when_to_use: Look up basic post metadata by post Id or a set of post Ids. | List posts with a resolved owner display name for display or reporting. | Serve as a stable base (grain = post Id) to join/add aggregates (comments, votes) or dimensions (tags, links) while avoiding duplication when done correctly. | Compose into higher-level queries that need post-level columns plus user display name without repeating owner-lookup logic.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the post — derived from posts.Id | Title: post title text — derived from posts.Title | OwnerUserId: foreign key referencing the user who owns the post (nullable) — derived from posts.OwnerUserId | OwnerDisplayName: resolved display name for the post owner — defined as COALESCE(posts.OwnerDisplayName, users.DisplayName) using posts.OwnerDisplayName and users.DisplayName
params.grounded_columns: posts.Id | posts.Title | posts.OwnerUserId | posts.OwnerDisplayName | users.Id | users.DisplayName
params.metric: Id = posts.Id | Title = posts.Title | OwnerUserId = posts.OwnerUserId | OwnerDisplayName = COALESCE(posts.OwnerDisplayName, users.DisplayName)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (or users table) on posts_core_52.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user so joining enriches post rows without duplicating them. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner (AGG) on posts_core_52.OwnerUserId = posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId — safe when posts_by_owner is aggregated per owner (one row per owner); it will not duplicate measures if you only select its aggregated columns. Be mindful when bringing aggregated counts into the same result (they are owner-level metrics repeated across that owner's posts by design). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup (NORM) on posts_core_52.Id = tags_lookup.PostId only if tags_lookup is one-row-per-post (it is a lookup — verify its grain). If tags_lookup is one-to-many (multiple tags per post), this will multiply post rows; instead, aggregate tags first (e.g., string_agg or tags-per-post AGG) before joining. | do NOT join directly to comments_per_post_agg (AGG) on posts_core_52.Id = comments_per_post_agg.PostId without verifying the agg grain: comments_per_post_agg is expected to be one-row-per-post (aggregated), so joining is safe — it will not duplicate measures. If instead you join to comments (raw) or any one-to-many comments table, you must first aggregate comments by post to avoid inflating post-level measures. | do NOT join directly to votes_per_post_agg (AGG) on Id if you instead join to raw votes table — raw votes is one-to-many and will multiply rows; always prefer the votes_per_post_agg view (one-row-per-post) or aggregate before joining. | do NOT join to postlinks_edges (JOIN) if it is one-to-many (multiple links per post) without aggregating first — joining a one-to-many edges table will duplicate post rows and any derived post-level measures. | When composing with rank-based sibling views (latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank): those rank views are typically one-row-per-post (or filtered subset). Joining on Id is safe provided the rank view is one-row-per-post; if the rank view contains multiple ranked rows per post, aggregate or filter to a single row (e.g., rank = 1) first. | When combining with badges_by_user or user_badge_counts (AGG) join on OwnerUserId = user id — safe because those are aggregated per-user (one row per user). Beware that per-user aggregates will be repeated across all posts by the same owner (this is expected when enriching each post with owner-level metrics). | General rule: safe joins are to tables/views that are one-row-per-post (key = posts.Id) or one-row-per-user (key = OwnerUserId). Avoid joining to any raw one-to-many detail (comments, votes, tags, links, posthistory) without first aggregating them to post-level or user-level to prevent duplicating post rows and inflating measures.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-post core attributes: Id, Title, OwnerUserId and a resolved OwnerDisplayName (post's stored name or the user's DisplayName).

views.name: posts_with_owner_display
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  COALESCE(u.DisplayName, p.OwnerDisplayName) AS effective_owner_displayname
FROM posts_with_owner p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id

params.description: Provides posts at the post (Id) grain with the post title and an effective owner display name (prefers users.DisplayName when available, otherwise falls back to the stored OwnerDisplayName on the post).
params.when_to_use: Look up a post's displayable owner name for presentation or reporting when you have a post Id or list of post Ids. | Compose queries that need a stable single-row-per-post representation including title and resolved owner name. | Joinable base for adding additional post-level measures (comments, votes, badges aggregated to the post owner) without duplicating post-level rows.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the post (derived from posts_with_owner.Id). | Title: the title of the post (derived from posts_with_owner.Title). | effective_owner_displayname: COALESCE(users.DisplayName, posts_with_owner.OwnerDisplayName) — the resolved display name to present for the post owner; uses users.DisplayName when a matching user exists, otherwise uses the OwnerDisplayName stored on the post.
params.grounded_columns: posts_with_owner.Id | posts_with_owner.Title | posts_with_owner.OwnerDisplayName | posts_with_owner.OwnerUserId | users.Id | users.DisplayName
params.metric: effective_owner_displayname = COALESCE(users.DisplayName, posts_with_owner.OwnerDisplayName)  -- expression that picks the user display name when a user row exists, otherwise falls back to the post's stored OwnerDisplayName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users (or users_core) on posts_with_owner.OwnerUserId = users.Id — safe because the view is one-row-per-post (grain = posts_with_owner.Id) and the LEFT JOIN to users in this view has already resolved the owner display name; joining again to the same users table on the same key will not duplicate post rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to normalized, one-row-per-entity views/tables keyed by post Id (for example latest_posthistory_per_post if it is one-row-per-post) on Id — safe because this view is one-row-per-post and those are also one-row-per-post. | do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many aggregates or detail tables (for example comments_per_post_agg is safe only if it is one-row-per-post; do NOT join to raw comments or other detail-level tables that are many rows per post) without re-aggregation, because joining a one-row-per-post view to a many-row-per-post table will multiply rows and effectively duplicate post-level measures. | do NOT join to any one-to-many sibling view (e.g., a raw comments table, posthistory detail, postlinks edges when used as edges with multiple rows per post) unless you first aggregate those tables to post-level (one row per posts_with_owner.Id) or use a DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER-based reduction; otherwise metrics derived at the post grain (here there are no numeric aggregates, but downstream aggregations expecting one row per post will be incorrect). | When composing metrics that count or sum (from other sources) per post, prefer joining this view to the corresponding per-post aggregate views in the sibling list (comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, posts_by_owner if appropriate) on Id — these aggregates are one-row-per-post or per-owner as documented, so they won't duplicate rows if keys align. If joining to an owner-level aggregate (e.g., badges_by_user aggregated to user), join on OwnerUserId = user key and re-aggregate at the desired grain to avoid duplication when multiple posts share the same owner.

views.description: Provides posts at the post (Id) grain with the post title and an effective owner display name (prefers users.DisplayName when available, otherwise falls back to the stored OwnerDisplayName on the post).

views.name: comments_by_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName,
  comments.Score AS Score
FROM comments

params.description: A row-level view of comments, one row per comment, exposing identifying, textual, temporal, user and score attributes.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve individual comment records or filter comments by post, user, date, or score. | Join comment-level detail to post or user entities when you need comment text, creation time, or score without aggregating. | Build aggregations (counts, averages, sums) over comments by post, user, time window, or other dimensions by composing with an aggregator view. | As a granular building block for analytics pipelines that need comment-level evidence (e.g., sentiment pipelines, text search, event timelines).
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the comment — derived from comments.Id | PostId: identifier of the post the comment belongs to — derived from comments.PostId | Text: full comment text content — derived from comments.Text | CreationDate: timestamp when the comment was created — derived from comments.CreationDate | UserId: identifier of the user who authored the comment (nullable) — derived from comments.UserId | UserDisplayName: display name provided on the comment (used when UserId is null or to show name snapshot) — derived from comments.UserDisplayName | Score: integer score (votes) for the comment — derived from comments.Score
params.grounded_columns: comments.Id | comments.PostId | comments.Text | comments.CreationDate | comments.UserId | comments.UserDisplayName | comments.Score
params.metric: Id = comments.Id | PostId = comments.PostId | Text = comments.Text | CreationDate = comments.CreationDate | UserId = comments.UserId | UserDisplayName = comments.UserDisplayName | Score = comments.Score
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic (or posts_with_owner) on comments_by_post.PostId = posts_basic.Id — safe because posts_basic is one-row-per-post; joining preserves one row per comment and does NOT duplicate comment rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on comments_by_post.UserId = users_core.Id — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user; joining preserves one row per comment. Note: UserId can be null; use LEFT JOIN if you want comments without a linked user. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup via posts (comments_by_post.PostId -> posts_basic.Id -> posts_basic.TagId or other post->tag relationship) only if that intermediate join is one-to-one; do NOT directly join comments_by_post to a many-to-many tags table without re-aggregation because that would duplicate comment rows. | do NOT join comments_by_post to any one-to-many aggregated children (for example, join directly to comments_per_post_agg is safe only if you join on PostId and treat the aggregate as additive per post — but joining comments_by_post to comments_per_post_agg on PostId will replicate the aggregate value for each comment of that post unless the intent is to see the aggregate repeated per comment). If you want per-post aggregates combined with comment-level rows without duplicating measures, join comments_by_post to the per-post aggregate on PostId and read the aggregate as a post-level attribute; be aware the aggregate will appear on every comment row for that post. | do NOT join comments_by_post to any view that is many-to-many with comments (for example, postlinks_edges or other edge tables that can have multiple rows per post) unless you first aggregate or deduplicate the target side. Joining to a many-to-many side will multiply comment rows and hence multiply any downstream sums/counts of comment-derived measures (e.g., Score). | If you need to compute totals or averages of Score safely after joining to a dimension that could duplicate rows, re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY comments_by_post.PostId SUM(Score) after the join) or join to pre-aggregated views (e.g., comments_per_post_agg) on PostId which are one-row-per-post.

views.description: A row-level view of comments, one row per comment, exposing identifying, textual, temporal, user and score attributes.

views.name: votes_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostId,
  UserId,
  VoteTypeId,
  BountyAmount,
  CreationDate
FROM votes

params.description: A normalized row-level view of every vote: one row per vote with its identifiers, type, optional bounty amount, and creation timestamp.
params.when_to_use: List or inspect individual votes (e.g., show votes for a given post or user). | Filter votes by type, date range, post, or user before aggregating (e.g., count votes, sum bounties). | Join to dimension views (posts, users, tags) when you need vote-level detail retained as one row per vote. | Build aggregated metrics grouped by PostId, UserId, VoteTypeId, CreationDate windows, etc., by composing aggregates on this view.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier for the vote row — derives directly from votes.Id | PostId: identifier of the post the vote is associated with — derives directly from votes.PostId | UserId: identifier of the user who cast the vote (nullable for anonymous/system votes) — derives directly from votes.UserId | VoteTypeId: numeric code representing the type of vote (e.g., upvote, downvote, accept, bounty) — derives directly from votes.VoteTypeId | BountyAmount: numeric amount awarded as a bounty for bounty-type votes (nullable otherwise) — derives directly from votes.BountyAmount | CreationDate: timestamp when the vote was created — derives directly from votes.CreationDate
params.grounded_columns: votes.Id | votes.PostId | votes.UserId | votes.VoteTypeId | votes.BountyAmount | votes.CreationDate
params.metric: vote_count = COUNT(Id)  -- straightforward count of rows in this view when aggregated | sum_bounty = SUM(BountyAmount)  -- sum of BountyAmount across filtered rows (NULLs ignored) | votes_by_type_count = COUNT(Id) FILTER (WHERE VoteTypeId = <value>)  -- conditional counts | first_vote_date = MIN(CreationDate)  -- earliest vote creation in an aggregation window | last_vote_date = MAX(CreationDate)  -- latest vote creation in an aggregation window
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic on votes_core.PostId = posts_basic.Id — safe because posts_basic is one-row-per-post (JOIN will not multiply vote rows; each vote has exactly one post). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner on votes_core.PostId = posts_with_owner.Id — safe for the same reason as posts_basic. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on votes_core.UserId = users_core.Id — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user; joining adds user attributes without duplicating vote measures (note: UserId can be NULL, use LEFT JOIN if you want to retain anonymous/system votes). | DO NOT join directly to votes_per_post_agg (AGG) expecting to preserve vote-level measures without care — votes_per_post_agg is one-row-per-post aggregate; joining it to votes_core on PostId is safe only if you understand you are adding pre-aggregated metrics per post to each vote row (this will repeat the same aggregated metrics for every vote of that post). If you intend to compute post-level aggregates, prefer aggregating votes_core itself (GROUP BY PostId) or join to votes_per_post_agg but avoid then re-aggregating across votes_core rows without deduplication. | DO NOT join to one-to-many views (e.g., comments_per_post_agg is aggregated per post so safe similar to votes_per_post_agg, but joins to genuinely one-to-many detail views would multiply vote rows). Specifically avoid joining to postlinks_edges (JOIN) or other edge/detail JOINs that are one-to-many from post to target without first aggregating the many-side, because they will duplicate vote rows and thereby overcount vote-derived measures unless you re-aggregate after the join. | If you need combined metrics at the post level that include both votes and another one-to-many relation (e.g., comments or postlinks), compute each side's aggregates separately (GROUP BY PostId on votes_core and on the other relation) and then join the aggregated results on PostId — this preserves cardinality and prevents measure multiplication. | When joining to RANK views (latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank), verify those views are one-row-per-post (or otherwise unique per join key). If they are one-row-per-post, they are safe to join on PostId; if they are multi-row per post (rank windows), either restrict to the intended single row (e.g., latest) or aggregate them first.

views.description: A normalized row-level view of every vote: one row per vote with its identifiers, type, optional bounty amount, and creation timestamp.

views.name: users_core_56
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName
FROM users

params.description: A one-row-per-user core lookup view exposing each user's Id and DisplayName.
params.when_to_use: Look up a user's display name given their Id | Join user identity information onto post/comment/vote data to show who authored an object | Serve as the dimensional user table when aggregating metrics by user (after aggregating measures on the many side) | Filter or group results by user attributes (Id or DisplayName)
params.output_schema: Id: the user's unique identifier — derived from users.Id | DisplayName: the user's chosen display name — derived from users.DisplayName
params.metric: Id = users.Id | DisplayName = users.DisplayName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic (or posts_with_owner, posts_by_owner) on users_core_56.Id = posts.ownerUserId — safe when you only need to attach user identity columns to each post row; this does not duplicate users_core_56 rows because posts are the many-side (one user to many posts) and the intent is to expand posts with user info. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to comments_per_post_agg on users_core_56.Id = comments_per_post_agg.UserId is NOT safe unless comments_per_post_agg is pre-aggregated to one row per user; comments_per_post_agg is an AGG over posts/comments (many-side) — joining it directly can duplicate users if comments_per_post_agg contains multiple rows per user. Instead, aggregate comments_per_post_agg to one row per UserId before joining. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to votes_per_post_agg only after ensuring it's reduced to one row per UserId (or join from the votes_agg keyed by UserId); direct join to a many-side votes table/view will multiply user rows and any user-level derived measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_badge_counts or badges_by_user on users_core_56.Id = user_badge_counts.UserId — safe because these sibling AGG views are expected to be one row per user (verify their grain). If those AGG views are one-row-per-user, they will not duplicate users_core_56 rows. | do NOT join to RANK or JOIN sibling views that are many-to-one into users_core_56 without re-aggregation: e.g., joining to latest_posthistory_per_post, postlinks_edges, posts_basic (if you intend to aggregate by user) or tags_lookup without handling the many-side will produce row multiplication. Always join this user core view as the dimension (one-side) and keep measures on the many-side aggregated before joining if you need user-level metrics. | recommended pattern for safe composition: (1) aggregate/compute metrics on many-side tables/views to one row per users_core_56.Id (e.g., SUM, COUNT grouped by ownerUserId/UserId), (2) then LEFT JOIN that aggregated result to users_core_56 on Id — this preserves one-row-per-user cardinality and avoids measure duplication.

views.description: A one-row-per-user core lookup view exposing each user's Id and DisplayName.

views.name: posts_core_57
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId
FROM posts

params.description: Row-level canonical projection of core post fields (Id, Title, Tags, ViewCount, OwnerUserId) for one-row-per-post queries and safe composition.
params.when_to_use: Fetch basic post attributes for a given post or set of posts by Id | Filter or select posts by OwnerUserId, Tag contents, Title or ViewCount and then join to other single-row-per-post views or aggregate over posts | Serve as the base input when computing aggregates per post (e.g., total comments per post) by joining to per-post aggregate views | Compose into analytics that need post metadata plus additional per-post metrics (views, comment counts, scores) without duplicating measures
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the post; derived from posts.Id | Title: post title text; derived from posts.Title | Tags: tag string for the post (usually delimited); derived from posts.Tags | ViewCount: number of times the post was viewed; derived from posts.ViewCount | OwnerUserId: user id of the post owner (may be null); derived from posts.OwnerUserId
params.metric: Id = posts.Id | Title = posts.Title | Tags = posts.Tags | ViewCount = posts.ViewCount | OwnerUserId = posts.OwnerUserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on posts_core_57.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user, so joining enriches post rows without duplicating post-level measures | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to comments_per_post_agg on posts_core_57.Id = comments_per_post_agg.PostId — safe because comments_per_post_agg is an aggregate already reduced to one row per post, so measures from posts_core_57 are not multiplied | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to votes_per_post_agg on posts_core_57.Id = votes_per_post_agg.PostId — safe because votes_per_post_agg is one-row-per-post aggregate | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner on posts_core_57.Id = posts_with_owner.Id — safe as posts_with_owner is a join that preserves one-row-per-post (verify it does not add multiple owner rows); use only if posts_with_owner is known one-row-per-post | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_posthistory_per_post on posts_core_57.Id = latest_posthistory_per_post.PostId — safe because latest_posthistory_per_post is rank-reduced to one row per post | do NOT join directly to comments (raw comments table) or any other one-to-many child table without first aggregating to one row per post (e.g., comments_per_post_agg), because joining a one-to-many table will duplicate posts_core_57 rows and multiply ViewCount and other post-level measures | do NOT join directly to postlinks_edges or postlinks (if they are many-to-many edges) unless you first aggregate or de-duplicate per-post, since those joins are potentially one-to-many and will multiply post rows | when composing further aggregations (e.g., SUM(ViewCount) by user), prefer to aggregate ViewCount from posts_core_57 after any joins that are guaranteed one-to-one; if you must join a one-to-many dimension, re-aggregate (GROUP BY posts_core_57.Id) to restore one-row-per-post before aggregating higher-level metrics

views.description: Row-level canonical projection of core post fields (Id, Title, Tags, ViewCount, OwnerUserId) for one-row-per-post queries and safe composition.

views.name: post_viewcount_agg_by_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS PostId,
  AVG(CAST(p.ViewCount AS REAL)) AS AvgViewCount,
  MIN(p.ViewCount) AS MinViewCount,
  MAX(p.ViewCount) AS MaxViewCount,
  COUNT(p.ViewCount) AS SampleCount
FROM posts p
GROUP BY p.Id

params.description: Aggregated view of view-count statistics per post (one row per post): average, min, max and sample count of Post.ViewCount.
params.when_to_use: When you need per-post summary statistics of the ViewCount metric (Avg, Min, Max, SampleCount). | When composing higher-level queries that need a single row per Post with pre-computed view-count aggregates (e.g., joining with post metadata, owner info, tags, scores) without re-aggregating view counts. | When comparing or filtering posts by their average/min/max view counts or by the number of view-count samples recorded.
params.output_schema: PostId: the primary identifier of the post; derives from posts.Id (GROUP BY key). | AvgViewCount: average of posts.ViewCount for that PostId; derived from AVG(CAST(posts.ViewCount AS REAL)). | MinViewCount: minimum posts.ViewCount for that PostId; derived from MIN(posts.ViewCount). | MaxViewCount: maximum posts.ViewCount for that PostId; derived from MAX(posts.ViewCount). | SampleCount: count of non-NULL posts.ViewCount values used in the aggregates for that PostId; derived from COUNT(posts.ViewCount).
params.metric: AvgViewCount = AVG(CAST(posts.ViewCount AS REAL)) | MinViewCount = MIN(posts.ViewCount) | MaxViewCount = MAX(posts.ViewCount) | SampleCount = COUNT(posts.ViewCount)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic (NORM) on posts_basic.Id = post_viewcount_agg_by_post.PostId — safe because both are one-row-per-post sources so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (NORM) or posts_with_owner (JOIN) on posts_with_owner.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id after first joining post_viewcount_agg_by_post to posts_with_owner by PostId or to posts_basic by PostId — safe when the join path is one-row-per-post to one-row-per-user (post -> owner) because post_viewcount_agg_by_post is one-row-per-post and will not be duplicated by a single owner row. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tags_lookup (NORM) only via a one-row-per-post intermediate that maps posts to a single tag (e.g., latest or primary tag) — otherwise joining directly to a many-to-many tag mapping will multiply rows and duplicate aggregates. If you need tag-level aggregates, first re-aggregate after joining: e.g., join post_viewcount_agg_by_post to post-tag mapping, then GROUP BY tag and apply aggregation (SUM/AVG/etc) on the aggregated metrics as appropriate. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many children such as comments_per_post_agg (if that view is one-row-per-post it can be safe) or to postlinks_edges, votes_per_post_agg, comments tables, or any many-row-per-post relationship without re-aggregation or ensuring a one-row-per-post join key. Direct joins to many-side tables will duplicate the post_viewcount measures and inflate/count incorrectly. | If you must combine with another per-post aggregate view (e.g., votes_per_post_agg, comments_per_post_agg, posts_by_owner), join on PostId — this is safe only if the other view is also strict one-row-per-post. Confirm sibling view grain before joining: both sides must be one-row-per-PostId to avoid duplication. | If combining into higher-level rollups (for example, computing owner-level average of AvgViewCount), re-aggregate the AvgViewCount appropriately (e.g., weighted by SampleCount if you need exact combined-average across raw samples). Example: OwnerAvg = SUM(AvgViewCount * SampleCount) / SUM(SampleCount) to compute a true average across all underlying ViewCount samples. | When joining to rank-based or top-N views (latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank), ensure those views remain one-row-per-post or restrict to a single rank row per post; otherwise de-duplicate before joining or re-aggregate after join.

views.description: Aggregated view of view-count statistics per post (one row per post): average, min, max and sample count of Post.ViewCount.

views.name: badges_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  UserId,
  Name,
  Date
FROM badges
WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL

params.description: One-row-per-badge-instance for badges that are associated with a user; answers who received which badge and when.
params.when_to_use: List badges awarded to users (Id, UserId, Name, Date) | Filter badges by user, badge name, or date and join to user-level data | Compose badge-level detail into user aggregates (after re-aggregation) | Build timelines of badges for a user or compute badge counts when aggregated appropriately
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the badge row (derived from badges.Id) | UserId: identifier of the user who received the badge (derived from badges.UserId) | Name: badge name/label (derived from badges.Name) | Date: date/time when the badge was awarded (derived from badges.Date)
params.metric: No derived numeric metrics in this view (all outputs are base columns). | If you need counts or other aggregates, derive them by aggregating UserId or Name after joining or grouping, for example: badge_count_per_user = COUNT(*) GROUP BY UserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on users_core.Id = badges_row_level.UserId — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user (this view is one-row-per-badge, so joining to the user dimension does not duplicate badge rows and retains one-row-per-badge granularity). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner (AGG) on posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId = badges_row_level.UserId — safe when you treat posts_by_owner as one-row-per-owner (pre-aggregated). It will not multiply badge rows because posts_by_owner is aggregated at the owner level and thus is one-row-per-user. | Do NOT directly join badges_row_level to one-to-many child tables/views such as posts_basic, posts_with_owner, comments_per_post_agg (if it is per-post), votes_per_post_agg (per-post), postlinks_edges, or latest_posthistory_per_post on non-unique keys without re-aggregation. Those joins can multiply badge rows because badges_row_level is one-row-per-badge and those other tables are one-to-many relative to the same user or unrelated post keys. | If you need user-level badge counts alongside one-to-many details (e.g., posts), either: (a) aggregate badges_row_level to user level first (e.g., SELECT UserId, COUNT(*) AS badge_count FROM badges_row_level GROUP BY UserId) and join that aggregate to the one-to-many table, or (b) join badges_row_level to the one-to-many table and then re-aggregate to the desired grain, ensuring you use GROUP BY on the intended keys to avoid double-counting. | Joining to badges_by_user (AGG) is redundant for counts (badges_by_user is already aggregated per user). Prefer using badges_by_user when you need pre-computed user badge aggregates; join on badges_by_user.UserId = badges_row_level.UserId only if you intentionally want both per-badge detail and per-user aggregates, and be mindful that this will attach the same aggregate value to multiple badge rows (no duplication of the aggregate itself, but duplicate propagation to multiple rows). | Joining this view to any RANK or AGG view that is keyed at a different grain requires aligning grains: ensure the join key is at the grain of the target (e.g., when joining to top_posts_by_score_rank which is per-post, join only on a post key — there is no post key in this badge view). | Summary: Safe to join on unique user dimension keys or other one-row-per-key aggregates. Avoid joining directly to one-to-many detail tables without first aggregating one side to the other side's grain or re-aggregating after the join.

views.description: One-row-per-badge-instance for badges that are associated with a user; answers who received which badge and when.

views.name: badges_per_user_aggregate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count,
  MIN(badges.Date) AS first_badge_date,
  MAX(badges.Date) AS last_badge_date
FROM badges
WHERE badges.UserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY badges.UserId

params.description: Per-user aggregated badge metrics: total badges and first/last badge dates for each user.
params.when_to_use: Report total number of badges a user has received | Filter or rank users by badge_count, earliest badge date, or most recent badge date | Join with user-level dimensions to enrich user profiles without duplicating badge counts | Compose into higher-level user summaries (e.g., combine with posts/comments aggregates) where one-row-per-user is required
params.output_schema: UserId: identifier of the user who received badges; derived from badges.UserId | badge_count: integer count of badge rows for that UserId; derived from COUNT(*) over badges rows per user | first_badge_date: earliest badge Date for that UserId; derived from MIN(badges.Date) | last_badge_date: latest badge Date for that UserId; derived from MAX(badges.Date)
params.metric: badge_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of badge rows grouped by badges.UserId | first_badge_date = MIN(badges.Date)  -- earliest badge.Date for the grouped UserId | last_badge_date = MAX(badges.Date)  -- latest badge.Date for the grouped UserId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on users_core.Id = badges_per_user_aggregate.UserId — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user (a dimension) so this view's user-level measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner on posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId = badges_per_user_aggregate.UserId — safe when combining user-level aggregates because posts_by_owner is an aggregated view that is one-row-per-owner; measures remain user-cardinality and will not be multiplied. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_badge_counts or badges_by_user on UserId only if those siblings are also one-row-per-user aggregates; safe because both are AGG siblings intended to be one-row-per-user (verify their grains match). | unsafe joins (do NOT join without re-aggregation): do NOT directly join to badges (base table) on badges.UserId = badges_per_user_aggregate.UserId because badges is one-to-many to users and will multiply badge_count and distort first/last dates unless you re-aggregate after the join. | unsafe joins (do NOT join without re-aggregation): do NOT join to posts_basic, posts_with_owner, comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, postlinks_edges, latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank, or tags_lookup if they are one-to-many relative to users — joining these raw or per-post/per-comment tables will duplicate rows and multiply badge_count. Instead, join only to their corresponding one-row-per-user aggregates (e.g., posts_by_owner) or aggregate after joining. | If you must combine with a one-to-many child (e.g., posts or comments), either: (a) aggregate the child to one row per UserId before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate at the UserId grain to compute correct combined metrics. This ensures badge_count remains correct and not duplicated.

views.description: Per-user aggregated badge metrics: total badges and first/last badge dates for each user.

views.name: users_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users
WHERE users.Id IS NOT NULL

params.description: A one-row-per-user normalized view exposing basic identifying attributes (Id, DisplayName) and simple metrics (Reputation, CreationDate) for each user.
params.when_to_use: Get top-level user attributes for display (profile cards, lists). | Filter or join users into queries that need a single row per user (e.g., attach owner info to posts). | Seed downstream aggregations or joins where you need stable user keys and basic user metrics.
params.output_schema: Id: the user's unique identifier — derives from base table column users.Id | DisplayName: the user's display name (string) — derives from base table column users.DisplayName | Reputation: the user's reputation score (integer) — derives from base table column users.Reputation | CreationDate: the timestamp when the user account was created — derives from base table column users.CreationDate
params.metric: Reputation = users.Reputation (pass-through column; not an aggregate) | CreationDate = users.CreationDate (pass-through timestamp)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic or posts_with_owner on posts.OwnerUserId = users_basic.Id — safe when you want to attach user attributes to each post (posts are the many side). This does not duplicate the users_basic row because posts are joined to users (one user row matched to many posts) and the measures in users_basic are per-user not aggregated across the join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner (AGG) on posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId = users_basic.Id — safe because posts_by_owner is pre-aggregated per-owner (one row per user); joining two one-row-per-user sources preserves cardinality and will not multiply measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to badges_by_user (AGG) on badges_by_user.UserId = users_basic.Id — safe when badges_by_user is aggregated per user (one row per user). | do NOT join directly to one-to-many objects such as comments_per_post_agg (AGG) or votes_per_post_agg (AGG) on non-matching keys without careful re-aggregation — for example, joining users_basic to comments_per_post_agg on post owner would multiply a user's row by the number of posts/comments unless the comments/votes side is aggregated to user level first. | do NOT join users_basic to postlinks_edges (JOIN) or latest_posthistory_per_post (RANK) without joining through posts_basic or an aggregation keyed to users_basic.Id; those views are post-centric and will produce multiple rows per user, which duplicates per-user columns if you expect one row per user. | When composing metrics that count or sum things per user, always aggregate the many-side by OwnerUserId (or UserId) before joining to users_basic. Example safe pattern: SELECT u.Id, u.DisplayName, p.post_count FROM users_basic u LEFT JOIN (SELECT OwnerUserId AS UserId, COUNT(*) AS post_count FROM posts_basic GROUP BY OwnerUserId) p ON p.UserId = u.Id — this preserves correctness and avoids multiplying user rows.

views.description: A one-row-per-user normalized view exposing basic identifying attributes (Id, DisplayName) and simple metrics (Reputation, CreationDate) for each user.

views.name: posts_with_owner_and_viewcount
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id,
  p.OwnerUserId,
  p.ViewCount,
  p.Title,
  p.Tags
FROM posts_core_57 p
WHERE p.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL

params.description: One-row-per-post (filtered to posts that have an owner) exposing post id, owner, view count, title and tags for downstream composition.
params.when_to_use: Get post metadata (title, tags, owner) and view count for individual posts or lists of posts | Join post-level metadata to user dimensions (owner) without changing post-level cardinality | Build post-level aggregations where view counts are needed as a base metric (e.g., sum of views by owner) provided downstream aggregations re-aggregate | Serve as the seed (base) view when composing further joins/aggregations that must start from one-row-per-post
params.output_schema: Id: primary key of the view; derives from posts_core_57.Id (the post identifier, grain = one row per post) | OwnerUserId: owner/author user id; derives from posts_core_57.OwnerUserId (nullable filtered to non-null in this view) | ViewCount: number of views for the post; derives from posts_core_57.ViewCount (stored metric on posts table) | Title: post title text; derives from posts_core_57.Title | Tags: tag string(s) associated with the post; derives from posts_core_57.Tags (likely a delimited/tagging column)
params.metric: ViewCount = posts_core_57.ViewCount (base column; treat as a numeric measure at post grain). No aggregation is applied in the view itself. When used in aggregated queries, it must be aggregated explicitly (e.g., SUM(ViewCount) to get total views over multiple posts).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on posts_with_owner_and_viewcount.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because posts_with_owner_and_viewcount is one-row-per-post and users_core is one-row-per-user; joining will not duplicate post-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic or posts_with_owner on Id = Id — safe when these sibling views are one-row-per-post (do not duplicate rows); use to bring additional post-normalized columns. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to latest_posthistory_per_post on Id = PostId (if latest_posthistory_per_post is RANK per post yielding one row per post) — safe because both sides are one-row-per-post. | DO NOT join directly (one-to-many) to comments_per_post_agg without aggregating comments_per_post_agg to one row per post first — comments_per_post_agg is an AGG at post grain (if it is one-row-per-post then it is safe), but if a sibling AGG were at a different grain or implemented as many rows per post, joining could multiply rows. Always confirm the sibling AGG's grain is post-level before joining. | DO NOT join to votes_per_post_agg or badges_by_user or posts_by_owner (if these siblings are multi-row per key) without ensuring they are reduced to one row per post or per owner respectively. For example, to get total votes per post, join to votes_per_post_agg only if that view is aggregated to one row per post (or join via a subquery that SELECTs SUM(votes) GROUP BY PostId). | When joining to user-level aggregates (e.g., badges_by_user, posts_by_owner): join on OwnerUserId = UserId only after ensuring the other side is one-row-per-user (aggregated) — joining a one-row-per-user aggregate is safe because it will attach user-level measures to each post once without duplicating post rows. | When attaching many-to-many relations (e.g., tags_lookup, postlinks_edges) be careful: tags_lookup likely maps tag names to tag ids and is many-to-one for tag metadata — joining on Tags string is not safe unless the tags column is normalized. postlinks_edges is a JOIN-sibling that can be many edges per post; do NOT join it directly without re-aggregation or a distinct/filter that preserves one row per post. | Planner guidance: treat this view as the post-level fact (grain = post). Any measure present here (ViewCount) is a post-level measure. To compute aggregates over users or tags, GROUP BY the desired higher-level key and aggregate ViewCount (SUM(ViewCount), AVG(ViewCount), etc.) rather than relying on joins that would multiply rows.

views.description: One-row-per-post (filtered to posts that have an owner) exposing post id, owner, view count, title and tags for downstream composition.

views.name: posthistory_counts_per_post_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PostId,
  UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS history_count
FROM
  postHistory
GROUP BY
  PostId,
  UserId

params.description: Per-post per-user counts of entries in postHistory (number of history rows for a given PostId and UserId).
params.when_to_use: Report how many postHistory entries a particular user has on a particular post (e.g., edits, revisions) when grouping by both PostId and UserId. | Joinable lookup when composing higher-level metrics that need history counts at the (PostId, UserId) grain (for example, attribute revisions on a post to its owner or to a specific editor). | Filtering or ranking posts by how many history events a specific user contributed to that post (when combined with filtering on UserId or PostId).
params.output_schema: PostId: the post identifier — sourced from postHistory.PostId | UserId: the user identifier — sourced from postHistory.UserId | history_count: count of postHistory rows for that PostId and UserId — computed as COUNT(*) over postHistory grouped by PostId and UserId
params.metric: history_count = COUNT(*) (count of rows in postHistory for the grouping keys PostId, UserId)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic (or posts_with_owner) on PostId — safe because posts_basic is one-row-per-PostId, so joining will not duplicate history_count rows; the view remains one row per (PostId, UserId) and history_count stays correct. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on UserId — safe because users_core is one-row-per-UserId (a dimension), so this lookup will not duplicate measures from this aggregated view. | do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many detail table (for example postHistory again, comments_per_post_agg without matching grain, postlinks_edges, votes_per_post_agg, or any table that has multiple rows per PostId or per (PostId,UserId)) without re-aggregating — such joins will multiply rows and therefore inflate history_count. If you need to combine with one-to-many data, either: | - aggregate the other table to the same grain (PostId, UserId) before joining, or | - join at a different grain and then re-aggregate (for example join to posts_by_owner aggregated at PostId and OwnerId and then aggregate to the desired grain), or | - perform the join and compute final measures using SUM(history_count) after grouping by the desired grain. | Examples of unsafe joins (will duplicate measures unless re-aggregated): join to posts_by_owner (if that view is multi-row per PostId), comments_per_post_agg (if aggregated per PostId only and you join by PostId expecting per-User counts), votes_per_post_agg, postlinks_edges, or any RANK view that can produce multiple rows per PostId — instead, aggregate those siblings to (PostId, UserId) or join via one-row-per-key dimensions first. | If you need history_count at the PostId-only grain, aggregate this view by PostId (SUM(history_count) GROUP BY PostId) rather than joining it to a PostId-level table which could multiply rows.

views.description: Per-post per-user counts of entries in postHistory (number of history rows for a given PostId and UserId).

views.name: badges_row_level_64
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  badges.Id AS Id,
  badges.UserId AS UserId,
  badges.Name AS Name,
  badges.Date AS Date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER) AS award_year
FROM badges

params.description: One-row-per-badge award: returns each row for a badge instance with its user, name, date, and extracted award year.
params.when_to_use: List badges with their award year for reporting or filtering (e.g., badges awarded in a given year). | Join badge-level data to user-level or post-level entities when you need badge occurrences (not aggregated counts). | Compose aggregations by award_year, UserId, or Name (e.g., badges per user per year) by aggregating this view.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the badge row — derived from badges.Id | UserId: foreign key referencing the user who received the badge — derived from badges.UserId | Name: name/type of the badge (string) — derived from badges.Name | Date: date/time when the badge was awarded — derived from badges.Date | award_year: integer year extracted from Date using CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER) — derived from badges.Date
params.metric: award_year = CAST(strftime('%Y', badges.Date) AS INTEGER)  -- derived scalar expression extracting calendar year from badges.Date
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on badges_row_level_64.UserId = users_core.Id — safe because badges_row_level_64 is one-row-per-badge and users_core is one-row-per-user; joining will not duplicate badge rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to badges_by_user (AGG) on badges_row_level_64.UserId = badges_by_user.UserId only if you understand badges_by_user is aggregated per user; joining an aggregate back to this row-level view is safe when you want the per-user aggregate repeated for each badge row (it does not alter the badge-row cardinality but repeats the aggregate value). | do NOT join badges_row_level_64 to posts_basic, comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, posts_by_owner, or any other one-to-many child (e.g., posts or comments) directly if you expect measures from badges_row_level_64 to remain unduplicated — those joins will multiply badge rows for each matching child row. If you must combine with one-to-many data, either: | - aggregate the one-to-many side to a compatible grain (e.g., per UserId or per PostId) before joining, or | - re-aggregate after the join to the desired grain to remove duplication. | example safe composition patterns: | - To compute badges per user per year: GROUP BY UserId, award_year over badges_row_level_64 (no join required). | - To attach user attributes: LEFT JOIN users_core ON badges_row_level_64.UserId = users_core.Id (safe). | - To attach per-user post counts: JOIN posts_by_owner (AGG) on UserId = posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId — safe because posts_by_owner is one-row-per-owner (aggregated) and will not change badge-row cardinality aside from repeating the aggregate.
