views.name: badges_by_year_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Name AS Name,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER) AS award_year,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count,
  MIN(Id) AS Id
FROM badges
GROUP BY Name, CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER)

params.description: Per-user, per-year counts of badges awarded (one row per user Name and award year).
params.when_to_use: How many badges did a given user earn in a specific calendar year? | Trend of badge counts per user across years (time series by award_year) | Compare badge totals across users for a single year | As an aggregated badge metric when joining to user dimension data (users_core) or further aggregating by year/cohort
params.output_schema: Name: display name of the badge recipient; derives from badges.Name | award_year: integer calendar year of the badge Date (CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER)); derives from badges.Date | badge_count: number of badge rows for that Name in that award_year; derives from COUNT(*) over badges grouped by Name and computed award_year | Id: representative badge Id for the group (the MIN(Id) among grouped rows); derives from MIN(badges.Id) and is not a count/measure of badges
params.metric: badge_count = COUNT(*)  -- count of badges for the grouping (Name, award_year) | award_year = CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER)  -- computed calendar year from badges.Date | Id = MIN(Id)  -- deterministic representative Id for the group; not a measure of volume
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on users_core.DisplayName = badges_by_year_cohort.Name — safe because badges_by_year_cohort is one-row-per (Name, award_year). Note: DisplayName->Name is not guaranteed unique in source data; only use this join if DisplayName equals Name and you accept potential many-to-one matches on the user side. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a year dimension (if present) on year_dim.year = badges_by_year_cohort.award_year — safe because the join is one-to-one or many-to-one from this view to the year dimension and does not duplicate badge_count. | do NOT join directly to posts_by_owner (AGG) or posts_basic (NORM) on Name/UserId without checking key semantics — joining on textual Name to a posts owner column may produce many-to-many duplication and multiply badge_count unless the join key is truly one-to-one. | do NOT join to comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, latest_posthistory_per_post, postlinks_edges, or posts_with_owner without re-aggregation: these are one-to-many or per-post views. If you need combined metrics, first aggregate those views to the same grouping keys (Name, award_year) or aggregate badges_by_year_cohort up to the join key level so that measures are aligned and not multiplied. | When composing into larger queries, preserve badge_count as an aggregate (SUM or AVG as appropriate) and avoid selecting raw badge_count and then joining to a child-table per (Name, award_year) — instead, join first on one-to-one dimensions or re-aggregate after the join to restore correct totals.

views.description: Per-user, per-year counts of badges awarded (one row per user Name and award year).

views.name: badges_total_per_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_count
FROM
  badges
GROUP BY
  Name

params.description: For each badge Name, the total number of badge rows with that Name (i.e., how many times that badge Name was awarded).
params.when_to_use: Get counts of how many times each badge name has been awarded (top-N badges by total_count). | Join badge counts to user or badge-detail dimensions (one-row-per-Name) without re-aggregation. | Compose with other aggregates (e.g., compute badge share among total badges) by joining on Name and then computing ratios. | Filter or rank badges by total_count (e.g., find badges awarded more than N times).
params.output_schema: Name: the badge name (derived from badges.Name). | total_count: the integer count of rows in the badges table for that Name (derived from COUNT(*) over badges rows grouped by Name).
params.grounded_columns: badges.Name | badges.* (COUNT(*) counts all rows from the badges table for each Name)
params.metric: total_count = COUNT(*) aggregated over badges rows grouped by badges.Name
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a one-row-per-Name dimension/view (if present) on Name — safe because badges_total_per_name is one row per Name so joined rows remain one-to-one and total_count is not duplicated. | Do NOT join badges_total_per_name directly to a one-to-many table keyed by Name (for example, if there existed a table listing multiple attributes per Name) without re-aggregation, because each matching attribute row would duplicate total_count. Instead either: |   - aggregate the many-side before joining (e.g., reduce it to one row per Name), or |   - join and then re-aggregate (e.g., SUM(total_count) grouped by original key) according to the intended final grain. | Safe joins to sibling views: |   - users_core (NORM): Safe only if joining on a column that guarantees one row per Name in users_core (users_core is per-user, so joining on Name is likely NOT safe unless users_core has a single row per badge Name—verify schema). |   - badges_by_user (AGG): Do NOT join badges_total_per_name to badges_by_user directly on Name without re-aggregating badges_by_user, because badges_by_user is per-user per-badge (one-to-many relative to Name) and would multiply total_count. |   - posts_basic, posts_with_owner, comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, posts_by_owner, latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank, postlinks_edges, tags_lookup: These are not keyed by badge Name. Do NOT join on Name to these views unless you first ensure a one-row-per-Name mapping (otherwise total_count will be duplicated). | General rule: badges_total_per_name's measure (total_count) is defined at the grain = Name (one row per Name). Any join that preserves that one-row-per-Name cardinality is safe; any join that produces multiple rows per Name must be followed by re-aggregation to avoid inflating total_count.

views.description: For each badge Name, the total number of badge rows with that Name (i.e., how many times that badge Name was awarded).

views.name: user_row
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.UpVotes AS UpVotes,
  users.Age AS Age
FROM users

params.description: Row-level user attributes: one row per user with their Id, UpVotes, and Age.
params.when_to_use: Fetch basic user attributes for a single user or a set of users by Id. | Join user-level attributes into higher-level analyses (e.g., posts or badges) while preserving one-row-per-user semantics. | Serve as the grounding (dimension) for user-level aggregations or filters (e.g., compute averages of UpVotes or Age across a user set).
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier for the user — derived from table users.Id | UpVotes: integer count of up-votes attributed to the user — derived from table users.UpVotes | Age: user's age (as stored) — derived from table users.Age
params.metric: Id = users.Id | UpVotes = users.UpVotes | Age = users.Age
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner (AGG) on posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId = user_row.Id — safe because posts_by_owner is pre-aggregated to one row per owner (OwnerUserId), so joining will not duplicate user_row measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to user_badge_counts (AGG) on user_badge_counts.UserId = user_row.Id — safe because user_badge_counts is aggregated per user (one row per UserId). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to badges_by_user (AGG) on badges_by_user.UserId = user_row.Id — safe when badges_by_user is aggregated to one row per user; confirm it is AGG before joining. | do NOT join directly to posts_basic (NORM) or posts_with_owner (JOIN) on posts_basic.OwnerUserId = user_row.Id without re-aggregation, because posts_basic is one-to-many (one user -> many posts) and will duplicate user_row measures unless you aggregate posts first (e.g., COUNT(posts.Id) grouped by OwnerUserId). | do NOT join directly to comments_per_post_agg, votes_per_post_agg, latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank, postlinks_edges, or tags_lookup unless you ensure those views are aggregated to one row per user or you aggregate after joining — they are either per-post, per-post-edge, or per-tag and can multiply the user rows if joined by post/tag keys. | safe composition pattern: if you need post-level details with user attributes, either (A) aggregate posts to user-level first (e.g., posts_by_owner) and join to user_row, or (B) join user_row to posts_basic and then re-aggregate the combined result using GROUP BY user_row.Id so the user-level measures remain correct. | note on measures: user_row exposes only raw user columns (no derived aggregates). Any metric aggregation (SUM, AVG, COUNT) over UpVotes or Age must be computed after joining if you join to one-to-many tables; to preserve correctness, perform aggregations grouped by user_row.Id.

views.description: Row-level user attributes: one row per user with their Id, UpVotes, and Age.

views.name: post_count_per_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(*) AS post_count
FROM
  posts
WHERE
  OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  OwnerUserId

params.description: Per-user count of posts: for each OwnerUserId, the total number of posts authored by that user (excluding NULL owners).
params.when_to_use: Get total posts by a specific user (e.g., user activity summary). | Rank or filter users by number of posts (top posters). | Join with user attributes to produce per-user reports combining profile and post volume. | Compose into higher-level metrics (e.g., posts per user per tag or posts-per-user augmented with comments) when starting from a per-user post total.
params.output_schema: OwnerUserId: the owner user identifier (derived from posts.OwnerUserId). | post_count: integer count of posts for that OwnerUserId (derived from COUNT(*) over posts rows where OwnerUserId is that value).
params.grounded_columns: posts.OwnerUserId | posts.* (COUNT(*) uses all rows in posts for counting)
params.metric: post_count = COUNT(*) over posts rows grouped by posts.OwnerUserId (SQL: COUNT(*) in the SELECT when grouping by OwnerUserId and excluding NULL OwnerUserId).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (or any one-row-per-user dimension) on OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because post_count is one value per OwnerUserId in this view and users_core provides at most one row per user, so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to badges_by_user (AGG, one row per user) on OwnerUserId = badges_by_user.UserId — safe because both sides are at the same OwnerUserId grain; joining preserves post_count without multiplication. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner (AGG) on OwnerUserId = posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId — safe only if you align/compare aggregated measures (both are one-row-per-owner), but avoid naive joins that expect to sum across both sides without re-aggregation. | do NOT join directly to posts (the base posts table) on OwnerUserId without re-aggregation — posts is many-to-one to this view (many posts per OwnerUserId), so a direct join will multiply post_count by the number of joined post rows and thus double-count measures. | do NOT join to comments_per_post_agg or votes_per_post_agg (which are aggregated per post) directly on post id via an intermediate posts join without re-aggregation — joining this per-user view to per-post aggregates through posts would create a one-to-many expansion (one user -> many posts -> many post-level aggregates) that duplicates the per-user post_count unless you re-aggregate after the join back to OwnerUserId. | when you need per-user metrics that combine this view with one-to-many details (e.g., total comments on that user's posts using comments_per_post_agg), join the per-post aggregate to posts (or posts_with_owner) first, then aggregate (SUM) the per-post metric grouped by OwnerUserId and finally join or compare to post_count. This ensures cardinality-safe composition by re-aggregating from post-level rows back to the OwnerUserId grain.

views.description: Per-user count of posts: for each OwnerUserId, the total number of posts authored by that user (excluding NULL owners).

views.name: votes_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.Id AS Id,
  v.PostId AS PostId,
  v.VoteTypeId AS VoteTypeId,
  v.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  CASE
    WHEN v.CreationDate IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE strftime('%Y', v.CreationDate)
  END AS creation_year
FROM votes v
WHERE v.CreationDate IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides one-row-per-vote records with vote attributes and the vote creation year, for votes that have a CreationDate.
params.when_to_use: Filtering or selecting vote-level details (Id, PostId, VoteTypeId, CreationDate). | Breaking down votes by year (creation_year) for time-based analyses or joins to yearly aggregates. | Joining vote-level data to post or user entities when you need per-vote granularity. | As a canonical, cleaned input when composing aggregates such as counts of votes per post/year or vote-type distributions.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the vote (derived from votes.Id) | PostId: identifier of the post the vote is attached to (derived from votes.PostId) | VoteTypeId: numeric code for the type of vote (derived from votes.VoteTypeId) | CreationDate: timestamp/date when the vote was created (derived from votes.CreationDate). Rows with NULL CreationDate are excluded by the view. | creation_year: four-digit year string extracted from CreationDate (derived by strftime('%Y', votes.CreationDate)); NULL when CreationDate is NULL (but such rows are already filtered out)
params.metric: creation_year = CASE WHEN votes.CreationDate IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE strftime('%Y', votes.CreationDate) END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic on posts_basic.Id = votes_cleaned.PostId — safe because posts_basic is one-row-per-post so joining brings post attributes into each vote row without duplicating vote-level measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_with_owner on posts_with_owner.Id = votes_cleaned.PostId — safe for the same reason (one-row-per-post). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core on users_core.Id = posts_with_owner.OwnerUserId after first joining posts_with_owner — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user; ensure you join posts_with_owner (one-to-one with posts) before users_core so vote rows map to a single user row. | cardinality-UNSAFE join warning: do NOT join directly to comments_per_post_agg (AGG) without aligning keys/aggregation if you expect to preserve vote-level cardinality — comments_per_post_agg is an aggregated, possibly one-row-per-post view; if it is one-row-per-post, joining on PostId is safe, but if it contains multiple rows per post (e.g., by commenter), it will duplicate vote rows. Confirm the sibling AGG's grain before joining. | cardinality-UNSAFE join warning: do NOT join to posts_by_owner (AGG) or badges_by_user (AGG) if those aggregates are one-row-per-(owner, metric) you intend to keep at vote granularity; joining an AGG that is one-to-many relative to posts or users can multiply vote rows. Instead, either join to a one-row-per-key normalization (e.g., posts_basic or users_core) or pre-aggregate/roll up the AGG to the same grain you need. | safe composition pattern: to compute votes-per-post metrics, first aggregate votes_cleaned (e.g., COUNT(*) GROUP BY PostId, creation_year, VoteTypeId) producing a one-row-per-PostId aggregate, then join that aggregate to posts_basic on PostId — this avoids duplicating measures. | safe composition pattern: to add post-level attributes while preserving vote counts, join posts_basic (one-row-per-post) to an aggregated result from votes_cleaned (one-row-per-post) rather than joining posts_basic directly to raw votes_cleaned when you want post-level metrics. | note on one-to-many siblings: sibling views labeled (AGG) or (RANK) may represent more-than-one-row-per-key. Treat them as potentially many-to-one or one-to-many; verify their documented grain before joining directly to votes_cleaned to avoid accidental multiplication of vote-level rows.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-vote records with vote attributes and the vote creation year, for votes that have a CreationDate.

views.name: votes_by_year_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS creation_year
FROM votes

params.description: Provides each vote Id and the calendar year (integer) when that vote was created.
params.when_to_use: Determine the distribution of votes by creation year (e.g., counts per year). | Filter or join votes by the year they were created when composing further analysis (e.g., join to posts or users while preserving one-row-per-vote identity). | As a building block for time-cohort analyses of votes where vote-level granularity is required.
params.output_schema: Id: unique identifier of the vote row — derives from votes.Id | creation_year: integer calendar year extracted from votes.CreationDate via CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER)
params.metric: creation_year = CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to votes_per_post_agg on votes_per_post_agg.PostId = <votes_by_year_cohort>.Id is NOT appropriate because votes_by_year_cohort.Id is the vote Id (not PostId); such a join would typically produce zero matches. Instead, to aggregate vote counts by year per post, first join votes_by_year_cohort to posts_basic (or posts_core) by matching the vote's PostId — NOTE: this view does not expose PostId, so to safely join to post-level tables you must use the base votes table or a sibling view that includes PostId (e.g., a normalized votes view that includes PostId). | Safe: join to a one-row-per-vote or one-row-per-Id view/table keyed on votes.Id (i.e., any normalized view exposing votes.Id) — safe because votes_by_year_cohort is one-row-per-vote (grain = Id), so no duplication of vote-level measures will occur when joining to another one-row-per-vote source on Id. | Safe: aggregate this view (e.g., COUNT(*) grouped by creation_year) before joining to one-to-many dimensions (posts, users, tags) — aggregating removes vote-level multiplicity so downstream joins will not multiply aggregated measures. | Do NOT directly join votes_by_year_cohort to one-to-many dimensions keyed on post/user without re-aggregation, because those joins would multiply rows and therefore inflate any counts or sums computed at the vote-grain. Examples of such one-to-many tables: posts_by_owner (one post owner -> many posts), comments_per_post_agg (many comments per post), badges_by_user (many badges per user). | If you need post-level measures (e.g., votes per post per year), compute aggregations from votes_by_year_cohort grouped by Id-of-interest (PostId) — since PostId is not in this view, obtain PostId from the base votes table or use a sibling view that includes PostId, then aggregate by (PostId, creation_year) to produce a one-row-per-(post,year) measure safe to join to post-level dimensions.

views.description: Provides each vote Id and the calendar year (integer) when that vote was created.

views.name: users_key
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users

params.description: Provides one-row-per-user identity and account linkage (Id, DisplayName, AccountId).
params.when_to_use: Look up basic user identity or display name by user Id | Join user identity onto posts, comments, badges, or other artifacts to attribute ownership | Compose with aggregations (e.g., counts per user) as the dimension in analyses by user | Filter or group results by AccountId or DisplayName when building user-level reports
params.output_schema: Id: unique user identifier — derived from users.Id | DisplayName: user's display name (display handle) — derived from users.DisplayName | AccountId: account-level identifier (can link users across sites/accounts) — derived from users.AccountId
params.metric: This view is purely a normalization (NORM) at the user grain and defines no aggregated metrics. No derived aggregate columns are present.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_basic or posts_with_owner on posts.OwnerUserId = users_key.Id — safe because users_key is one-row-per-user, so joining the user dimension to a one-to-many fact (posts) will replicate the user row per post (expected) but will not duplicate any pre-aggregated user measures (there are none). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to badges_by_user or user_badge_counts on user_badge_counts.Id = users_key.Id — safe because badges_by_user/user_badge_counts are already aggregated per user; joining them to users_key (1:1 by Id) will not multiply badge counts. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to posts_by_owner on posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId = users_key.Id — safe because posts_by_owner is aggregated per owner; this is a 1:1 join from users_key to that aggregate so metrics remain correct. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to one-to-many child tables (e.g., comments, posts, votes_per_post_agg if used at post-grain) when you expect to preserve user-level aggregates — joining users_key (1 row) to a raw one-to-many table (comments, posts) will produce multiple rows per user and will multiply any measures derived prior to the join. If you require user-level metrics after such a join, re-aggregate (GROUP BY users_key.Id) or use the corresponding per-user aggregate views (e.g., user_badge_counts, posts_by_owner). | do NOT join to rank or per-post/per-item aggregates (latest_posthistory_per_post, top_posts_by_score_rank, votes_per_post_agg, comments_per_post_agg) and expect user-level aggregates to remain unchanged unless you first aggregate those per-user (e.g., sum votes per owner) or join through a one-to-one mapping (e.g., join posts -> owner then aggregate). | safe composition pattern examples: (a) to get total posts per user, join posts_by_owner (aggregated) to users_key on users_key.Id = posts_by_owner.OwnerUserId; (b) to attach display names to post-level rows, join posts_basic.OwnerUserId = users_key.Id (this expands users into posts as expected).

views.description: Provides one-row-per-user identity and account linkage (Id, DisplayName, AccountId).

views.name: posts_by_owner_aggregate
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(Id) AS PostCount,
  SUM(COALESCE(ViewCount, 0)) AS TotalViewCount
FROM posts
GROUP BY OwnerUserId

params.description: Per-owner aggregates of number of posts and total views (one row per OwnerUserId).
params.when_to_use: Get total posts and total view counts for each owner/user (OwnerUserId) for reporting or leaderboard purposes. | Compose owner-level metrics into richer owner profiles by joining to one-row-per-user dimensions (e.g., users_core or badges_by_user aggregated to one row). | Filter or rank owners by activity (PostCount) or reach (TotalViewCount) before joining to other owner-level datasets. | Act as the aggregated base when computing rates (e.g., average views per post = TotalViewCount / PostCount) — compute derived metrics from these columns.
params.output_schema: OwnerUserId: the owner/user identifier; sourced from posts.OwnerUserId (GROUP BY key). | PostCount: number of posts for that OwnerUserId; derived from COUNT(posts.Id). | TotalViewCount: total view count across posts of that OwnerUserId; derived from SUM(COALESCE(posts.ViewCount, 0)).
params.metric: PostCount = COUNT(posts.Id) -- a COUNT aggregate over the base row identifier Id per OwnerUserId. | TotalViewCount = SUM(COALESCE(posts.ViewCount, 0)) -- a SUM aggregate of the ViewCount column (nulls treated as 0) per OwnerUserId.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to users_core (or any one-row-per-user view/table) on posts_by_owner_aggregate.OwnerUserId = users_core.Id — safe because users_core is one-row-per-user, so joining does NOT duplicate PostCount or TotalViewCount. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to badges_by_user (if it is pre-aggregated to one row per user) on OwnerUserId = badges_by_user.UserId — safe only if badges_by_user is aggregated to one row per user; otherwise it will duplicate measures. | do NOT join directly to posts (the original table) on OwnerUserId without re-aggregating the posts side (or dropping the aggregated measures), because posts is one-to-many to OwnerUserId and will multiply PostCount and TotalViewCount. | do NOT join to one-to-many child aggregates (e.g., comments_per_post_agg joined via post id) without ensuring the join path preserves one-row-per-OwnerUserId (you must either re-aggregate after the join or join through a one-row-per-owner intermediate). Joining a per-post aggregate to this per-owner aggregate on OwnerUserId by first expanding posts will duplicate owner-level metrics. | safe composition pattern: to combine per-owner post metrics with per-post metrics (e.g., comments_per_post_agg or votes_per_post_agg), first aggregate the per-post metrics to owner level (GROUP BY OwnerUserId) and then join those owner-level aggregates to posts_by_owner_aggregate on OwnerUserId — this avoids double-counting. | safe composition pattern: to compute averages or ratios that combine counts, compute them using the provided aggregates (e.g., AverageViewsPerPost = TotalViewCount / NULLIF(PostCount,0)) rather than by joining back to posts. | note on sibling ranked/joined views: do NOT join directly to ranked/per-post views like top_posts_by_score_rank or latest_posthistory_per_post unless those views are reduced to exactly one row per OwnerUserId; ranked views are typically per-post and will cause duplication unless further aggregated.

views.description: Per-owner aggregates of number of posts and total views (one row per OwnerUserId).
